name: FAA NTSB Safety Recommendations System
description: Within the FAA Line of Business known as Aviation Safety (AVS), the Office of Accident Investigation and Prevention (AVP) is the principal organization that investigates aviation accidents and trends in the National Airspace System (NAS) and coordinates the corrective action process. AVP, located in the FAA Headquarters Building in Washington, D.C, serves as the primary liaison between the FAA and the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB). The Recommendations Branch (AVP-120) uses two processes to handle safety recommendations, one for FAA Safety Recommendations and one for NTSB Safety Recommendations. Supporting these processes are Recommendations Branch employees and a single, robust repository application known as the FAA and NTSB Recommendations System, or FNRS. AVP assigns all accepted safety recommendations to the appropriate program office with subject matter responsibility, such as the Flight Standards Service (AFX) and the Aircraft Certification Service (AIR), to be reviewed and processed throughout the recommendation’s lifecycle.

description:

This tool enables Program Offices to request task codes to be set up in Delphi for Facilities and Equipment (F&E) and Operations (OPS) Capital Projects so that their projects can be activated for correct accounting treatment.  This tool is available to all Headquarters and Technical Center Program Offices for processing their requests.  
Regional Capitalization Teams also use this tool to determine whether their associated projects should be set up as capitalized or expensed. Utilizes documentum for storage.

name: Specials and Waivers Inventory Management System
fullname_0: Specials and Waivers Inventory Management System
description:
The Specials and Waivers Inventory Management System (SWIMS) supports the Flight Technologies
and Procedures Division (AFS‐400) with the creation, review, and analysis involved with document
packages for each flight instrument procedure requests received. This system allows several kinds of
users, each corresponding with a specific team function, to track and modify these packages from
the initial receipt to the final approval or disapproval and/or distribution. The SWIMS process begins
with the receipt of instrument flight procedure requests from external procedures developers. Users
assigned as Administrators create and manage a Package Tracking Record (PTR) to monitor all
activity conducted through the review and authorization processes by reviewers and managers
within the system boundaries. Users provide required information to ensure data accuracy and
currency. External organizations, all outside of AFS‐400, have access to SWIMS and are provided
information based on their role/function. Throughout these life cycles, users can search records
and generate reports.

name: Virtual Reality Tools
description:
The FAA’s Power Services Group (PSG) AJW-22 has developed the Virtual Reality Tools (VRT), which facilitates delivery of high-quality virtual reality modules for purposes of PSG training and tower siting assessments but will be more broadly scoped in future to accommodate a wider range of FAA training needs.  The VRT accurately replicates workspaces, offering FAA employees and contractors an immersive, collaborative platform to get hands-on experience undertaking tasks – and ultimately – offers a risk-free space to develop skills needed to work in dangerous environments, or with hazardous equipment without being exposed to real world dangers.  

The VRT is comprised of two custom applications built by Brightline Interactive (BLI) using FAA-approved hardware and software: 

(1) Eaton 93 Power Module (PM) Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS) – includes seven (7) modules built by BLI.  Users are PSG personnel with PSG-specific training requirements.  Users login to system using PIV/MyAccess on FAA GFE laptops and interface with training modules via Virtual Reality (VR) head mounted display (HMD) peripheral devices. 

(2) Virtual Immersive Siting Tower Assessment (VISTA) 3D modeling – used for the terminal facilities siting process.  Virtual reality allows for collaboration among users to plan for the construction of new air traffic control towers and terminal radar approach controls.  VISTA will be used by both FAA personnel and other facilities/air traffic control stakeholders.  Users login to system using PIV/MyAccess on FAA GFE laptops and interface with VISTA via VR HMD peripheral devices.

name: Voluntary Disclosure Reporting Program
description: VDRP is a web-based application that supports the FAA and the Office of Aviation Safety (AVS) Flight Standards Service (AFS) with the online acquisition, storing, sorting, aggregating, retrieving, reviewing, analyzing, and reporting of VDRP information from multiple airlines and other Regulated Entities. The Voluntary Disclosure Reporting Program (VDRP) allows Regulated Entities such as air carriers, repair stations, and Production Approval Holders (PAH), to voluntarily disclose inadvertent violations of Federal Aviation Regulations (FAR) to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The program provides for the collection, analysis, and retention of safety data that would otherwise be unobtainable. Ultimately, the safety data, which is collected and analyzed, will be used to develop corrective actions for identified safety concerns and to educate the appropriate parties to prevent a recurrence of events with the same root cause. By voluntarily submitting a violation, the Regulated Entity limits its exposure to the sanctions normally associated with such violations.

name: Integrated Safety Assessment Model
description: ISAM is a web-based platform developed to estimate the risk in the air transportation safety system. ISAM estimates risk by modeling key aspects of the air transportation safety system from multiple perspectives (systems, equipment, operations, management, and system users — i.e., pilots, air traffic controllers, maintenance, etc.) and by integrating these aspects together to form a total risk picture of the safety system. This knowledge enables engineers, managers, and policy makers to make more informed decisions about the priority, timing, safety benefits and impacts of operational changes. It is a decision support tool using Event Sequence Diagrams and Fault Trees.

name: ASH Internal Web Portals
description:
ASH Web Portals is a central data repository containing ASH Security & Hazardous Material mission support data. Its purpose is to provide single sign-on functionality, making the web portal a single location from which to be authenticated for access to a number of individual applications which support FAA personnel security, FAA physical security, and HAZMAT operations. Key applications which are accessed on the ASH Web Portal are: Facility Security Reporting System (FSRS), Personnel Access System (PASS), Security Information Reference System (SIRS), Security Awareness Virtual Initiative for Facility Security (ASH SAVI), and others. It is anticipated that additional user applications will be added as needed. Operational at FAA Headquarters in Washington DC.
ASH Web Portals provides single sign-on functionality for ASH employees and contractors to access certain applications from within the internal FAA network (including FAA Remote Access Control Virtual Private Network) to several applications.  Currently, the applications accessed on ASH Web Portals are:
Aviation Hazmat Portal (AHP) – Supports Hazardous Materials and Enforcement Program
Classified/CUI – Used to access COMSE and FSRS 
COMSEC – Used by Security Service Elements in HQ and in the field for tracking COMSEC inspections
Conference Room Scheduling –Internal calendar application to schedule ASH conference rooms
Credentials (Dialogic Board) – Issues credentials to DOT and FAA  track employees. Interactive Voice Response system to receive phone calls - it locates and speaks out the credential information to field agents. 
Employee Contractor Verification System (ECVS) – Used to verify the status of an individual in the event they need to access a facility and do not have their PIV card with them
Executive Information System (EXIS) – A project management tracking system providing an overview of ASH projects
Facility Security Reports System (FSRS2/ FSRS) – Information management system designed to capture, process, and report information related to FAA facilities, physical security assessments, comprehensive and supplemental inspections, communications security, classified/CUI, incidents, accreditation, quarterly reports, and inspector reports
Gov Vehicle – Vehicle scheduling application used in the southern region
International Travel Follow-up Questionnaire – Application (survey) developed for AXI to gather security related information regarding international travel
International Visitor Program (IVP) – Web-based application that processes data from international visitors seeking approval to visit FAA facilities using FAA Form 1600.78.  Once submitted the data is used by the FAA Office of International Affairs (API) to review the visit and forward it to AXM, ASH Service Area personnel, and the appropriate Line of Business for review.  ASH Service Area personnel forward the visit request to the appropriate FAA facility manager for approval.
Leave Scheduler – For ASH personnel to track leave
Personnel Access Security System (PASS) –Permits the creation and management of user accounts required for access to the Portals and other ASH applications
SEAD 3 (Senior Executive Agent Directive) Reporting Tool –Provided to support Departments and Agencies with the implementation of the Security Executive Agent Directive
Web Incident Reporting (WEBIRs) – Website used by employees and contractors to report incidents at or near FAA facilities
ASH Web Portals also provides access to various internal ASH and FAA information sources, including:
ASH Directory
Users attempting to access ASH applications are authenticated via MyAccess, an AIT application, using either a user name and password or a fully enabled PIV card with a Personal Identification Number (PIN).

There is no other user-input capability into the FAAMIS system, which is classified as an FAA “System of Record.”

name: Enterprise Data Platform
description:
Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Enterprise Information Management (EIM) is part of the next-generation evolution of moving the FAA community from a program-centric model to a high-performance shared data enterprise. EIM supports the FAA's mission by integration through a unified data layer leveraging a secure cloud's processing power combined with a set of analytical and visualization tools EIM enables a common open platform empowered with a set of industry COTS products to realize the true potential of FAA data and enable the next level of agency safety and efficiency. 
 EIM enterprise model designed to rapidly scale on-demand to meets variation in existing and emerging data. EIM build to meet the FAA's diverse internal and external stakeholders' information management requirements while providing a common enterprise access model that is continuously refined to empower and encourage users in terms of creation, rapid decision-making, and increased mission agility.  The FAA processes extensive data sets, typically many terabytes per day. There is also a need to implement and manage a diverse set of data access, handling, and dissemination policies concerning operational data, personally identifiable information (PII), and other sensitive or restricted data. 
  A comprehensive and integrated security framework with configurable security policies is required to address these needs and enable programs/applications to easily connect to a platform and inherit the security features, services, and authorizations of the Enterprise Capability (EC).

name: Aviation System Performance Metrics
description:
Aviation System Performance Metrics (ASPM) was established as a collaborative effort to reduce delays. It's an analysis tool to provide information on key delay indicators, airport efficiency, predicted and actual arrival and departure rates, enroute efficiency, taxi-times, individual flight performance, and cancellations. The data is updated daily. ASPM provides statistics for 77 airports as well as system statistics for all domestic airports with scheduled data. The system includes  OPSNET Reports, PERTI Assessment Tool, NAS Daily Report, NAS AERO Report, NAS Recap, and KPI Report).  
 Traffic Flow Management System Counts (TFMSC) is part of ASPM and is designed to provide information on traffic counts by airport or by city pair for various data groupings such as aircraft type or by hour of the day.  It includes data for flights that fly under Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) and are captured by the FAA’s enroute computers. Most VFR and some non-enroute IFR traffic is excluded. TFMSC source data are created when pilots file flight plans and/or when flights are detected by the National Airspace System (NAS), usually via RADAR.

The ASPM system is a set of servers to:
• Retrieve and/or accept data from the many input sources
• Process and manipulate that input data
• Store and/or insert that processed data into databases
• Facilitate the reporting of that data

ASPM also receives data from outside sources for daily operations, including next day Out, Off, On, In (OOOI) data, Diversions, and next day Automated Surface Observing System (ASOS) weather data.

name: National Airspace System Status
description:
Public application that provides current and forecast information for traffic management initiatives.

Currently the FAA maintains a public web page called fly.faa.gov. This web page provides information to the flying public about traffic management initiatives that are ongoing in the National Airspace System (NAS). This website has been in existence for over 20 years and is maintained with other NAS mission critical systems and is fed data directly from those systems. It is the goal of the FAA to move this function from its current location and into a cloud environment where it can be fed public System Wide Information Management (SWIM)ata. 

The NAS Status website serves as the new replacement
tool for the fly.faa.gov web page. The existing fly.faa.gov website serves as a central place for users to view impactful information in the National Airspace such as National Programs, Arrival and Departure Delays, Flight Restrictions, etc. The goal of the new website is to efficiently process and display the same FAA data for the flying public, including pilots, schedulers, dispatchers, etc in a way that makes it easier for end users to make decisions about their light operations. The new website also aims to exemplify FAA’s ability to deploy cloud native software that can be maintained and updated by the FAA itself on the AIT Container Platforms system in the FCS.  The new website URL is https://nas.faa.gov.

name: Facilities Management Website
description:
The Facility Management Website (FMW) is open to ALL employees/contractors who have access to the internal FAA enterprise network infrastructure via their PIV. FMW is a portal that consists of several components that provide services to FAA employees/contractors. 

The web-based FAA Transit Benefits Application (FTBA) provides a service to FAA participants (employees only) for them to request and manage their Transit Benefits.  The web-based FAA Parking Application (FPA) provides a service to ALL employees/contractors for them to request and manage permanent parking at FAA. The participants parking application must be authorized by the participants manager and/or LOB/SO POC and then is processed by the Facilities Management Customer Service Center (CSC) staff. Additionally, the FAA Service Call Ticket System (FSTS) provides a process for all employees/contractors to be able to make & manage a service request through the CSC.

FPA interacts with FTBA (and vice/versa) in accordance with federal law as participants can only receive one type of benefit. FPA/FTBA performs a check to ensure participant is not currently receiving benefit when the respective application is submitted by participant. All web-based applications intact with the FAA relay email server to provide email confirmation and/or notifications.

11/29/23 - Detailed info provided by Elaine Rodgers concerning tech upgrades:

Task: Comment on the reason Microsoft Edge IE Mode is presently on hold.
Comment: The WebOPSS Release 1.3.0 (now on hold) partly was to implement the Browser Compatibility Enhancements (BCE) for Google Chrome and Microsoft(MS) Edge to replace MS IE Mode.   
Response:  AFS 260 requested on September 5, 2023,  to hold the Release 1.3.0 Browser Compatibility Enhancement (BCE) release which includes replacement of the MS IE Mode deployment.   The request was based primarily on the template development functionality not working properly, current production release issues, and the IE Mode compatibility with Windows 11. There is no target date for deployment of the BCE release at this time.

Issues to Resolve: 
Priority one – Production Issues.  Interim Releases (Release 1.2.11, 1.2.12, and Release 1.2.13 (TBD)) to implement fixes for defects and infrastructure upgrades.
Priority two - Template Development.  WebOPSS relies on a third party tool (Telerik) to support template development.  The latest version of Telerik UI for ASP.NET AJAX  introduced a number of limitations and functionality issues with the template development.  There are limitations that may be addressed in a not yet offered/released version of Telerik. There are some work arounds recommended, but not sufficient for day to day operations. 
Priority three – Browser Compatibility Enhancements (BCE) release include the upgrade of MS IE Mode to MS Edge. According to MS Edge Lifecycle: ‘Microsoft is committed to supporting Internet Explorer mode in Microsoft Edge through 2029, on supported operating systems. Additionally, Microsoft will provide a minimum of one year notice prior to end of support for IE mode.’  AIF-500 provided confirmation ‘based on the need of many at the FAA’; the support for IE Mode will continue through end of life support by Microsoft through at least 2029. 
Priority four – WebOPSS IE Mode compatibility with Windows 11. The current WebOPSS production release MS IE Mode only worked with Windows 10.  MS deployed a patch for Windows 11.  WebOPSS production release was tested and works with Microsoft Windows 11.
name: Web Based Operations Safety System
description: WebOPSS is a mission-critical regulatory system that develops, records, and tracks safety authority from the FAA and economic authority from the OST granted under Title 49 USC and required for all commercial air operators and air agencies. WebOPSS houses the legal documents that are the conditions and limitations that air operators and agencies must follow e.g., operational specifications, management specifications, training specifications, letters of authorization. These conditions and limitations are extensions of FAA regulations and are specific to the individual air operator or agency. WebOPSS also allows commercial air carriers to electronically draft changes to specifications, digitally sign them and present them to the FAA. WebOPSS is the ONLY authoritative source for all operations safety specification and other authorizing documents that are mandated under Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR). WebOPSS is also critical component for the implementation of NextGen authorizations for use of new technologies and procedures, such as NAV Lean Program. Specialized WebOPSS Tier-3 Support is required due to the criticality of the documents issued through WebOPSS.

3/29/23 - Update per Lai Lee-Birman to Scott Dalaba - Silverlight is needed until the legacy SPAS application is decommissioned after the SPAS Modernization version 3.2 release, which is currently scheduled to be completed at the end of 2024.  A Risk Acceptance Waiver for Microsoft Silverlight Software for SPAS was submitted to AIS on October 26, 2022.  
8/11/2022:  Update from Scott Dalaba:  After discussions with the AIF Client Imaging team, AIF will perform the following to continue to support SPAS with Silverlight.
AIF will add Microsoft Silverlight onto the 21H2 image to support SPAS with Silverlight.
AIS Team members – Is there any tasks required to document the continued requirement for use of Microsoft Silverlight in support of SPAS?


8/2/2022 (Note from Scott Dalaba re: Silverlight) :

Silverlight went End of Life by Microsoft on 10/15/2021.
As of January 2022, the Windows 10-21H2 image and the Windows 11-21H2 image do not have Silverlight installed.  AIF is unable to download it anymore from Microsoft (since it is End of Life).
AIF will reach out to Microsoft for any options and see if we can obtain the software again.
If AIF can, we can setup the software as a self-service install through Tanium, so not every computer has it.

So my understanding is only AVS requires this application?  So let’s review possible scenarios that can occur from now until the retirement of SPAS (sometime in 2024/2025).

Scenario 1:  If the customer is updated from 20H2 to 21H2 and they previously had Silverlight installed, it will still be installed.

Scenario 2:  Customer receives a LCM/Break-Fix/New Hire -  Silverlight is not provided on the updated 21H2 image.  

Is AIS aware of the dependency and the issues it is causing?  Is the Program office aware?
There will need to be a Risk Acceptance developed/accepted by AVS that identifies the vulnerability and AIS will need to accept the risk.
I would request the System Owner reach out to AIS (start an AIS Intake) to begin the process.

AIF timeline for Windows 21H2 Deployment  (Windows 10-20H2 is unsupported after 5/10/23)
•	AIT Pilot – starts today (Tue 8/2/22)
•	ECMB Approval – Week of 8/8
•	Enterprise deployment to begin week of 8/22 or 8/29

I’ve also added the End of Life Technologies Team for their awareness.
Any questions, please let Chris C or I know.
Thanx 
Scott Dalaba

name: API Center for Excellence
description:
The mission of the API C4E is to provide an enterprise level IT service that enables you to work smarter by building your own API’s.  To realize this mission, the API Center for Enablement (API C4E) provides the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) with a service-oriented architecture middleware technology solution for developing, operating, and publishing Application Programming Interfaces (APIs).  The APIs belong to three broad categories: client APIs, business process APIs, and system level APIs.  Client APIs are developed to meet specific client application requirements.  Business process APIs encapsulate repeatable business processes to share and re-use with the Client APIs.  Finally, the system APIs connect to back-end systems, like databases, and allows the business process APIs to integrate with other IT systems.  Each layer requires different considerations for security controls.
APIs published within the API C4E may be intended for multiple audiences.  Many are specifically for internal FAA use, some are available to coordinate with industry partners, and finally, some are available to the general public.
In order to support the enterprise to develop, operate, and publish APIs, the API C4E utilizes the Mulesoft platform, which is a commercial product designed to provide a full-service API management solution.  This platform includes multiple components, hosted in several different places.
•	The Mulesoft Anypoint Platform
o	The primary “control plane” component of the Mulesoft system.  This component is used to for administration work.  This work includes applying security policies, performing monitoring, and performing other maintenance activities.  This component also coordinates the various “runtime planes” (see below).  This component is fully hosted by Salesforce (the parent company that owns Mulesoft) and runs within their infrastructure.
•	The Mulesoft Runtimes
o	The runtime allows APIs developed using the Mulesoft low-code development tools to actually execute.  Similar to Microsoft’s Internet Information Services (IIS) for .Net code, or Apache Tomcat for Java code, the runtimes are deployed to containers within the FAA’s FCS AWS cloud.
•	The API Community Manager
o	This is a web portal that publishes metadata about all APIs available.  An FAA employee, FAA contractor, industry partner, or member of the public may request access to browse the catalog.  Within the catalog, there are tools that allow these users to submit a further request for access to the actual API.  These requests may have different requirements for permission to access based on the sensitivity and availability of the API, determined by the line of business who owns the underlying system.

The basic capabilities must include an API gateway to secure and monitor APIs, an API catalog to allow for publication and discovery of APIs, and development tools to allow rapid development with data connectors and process automation flows. name: Cost Accounting System
description:
The FAA Cost Accounting System (CAS) uses the PeopleSoft (PS) Projects and GL modules for allocations. expenses, revenues, gain and losses data is interfaced  through DTF into PS from the Agency accounting system (DELPHI) via a front-end-control system (FECS). The results of allocations processed in PeopleSoft are extracted, and loaded into a data warehouse named PURE. CAS uses Business Objects to provide CAS reports from the data warehouse. FAA users can access CAS reports from PURE. These reports provide FAA executives and managers a better understanding of the full cost of FAA products and services delivered. CAS is also used to calculate standard labor rates for reimbursable work, cost recovery rates–overflight fees, indirect rates for reimbursable agreements, produce Statement of Net Cost for the Agency's Performance and Accountability Report (PAR) and compute programs lifecycle costs.

FAA began developing its cost accounting system in 1996, as directed by the Federal Aviation Reauthorization Act of 1996 ("The Act"). The Act required the agency to develop a system that
adequately and accurately reflected the investments, operating and indirect costs, revenue, other financial measurements and reporting aspects of its operations. CAS has evolved, in response to
continuing guidance, to enable the agency to meet the requirements and recommendations of both external and internal parties.

name: Air Traffic Control Specialist Auxiliary Information Display
fullname_0: Air Traffic Control Specialist Auxiliary Information Display
description: AAID provides information for the operations floor that is similar to the En Route Information Display System (ERIDS). Anchorage Center is not part of the En Route Automation Modernization (ERAM) that the rest of the Air Route Traffic Control Centers (ARTCC) use, so AAID was kept in service rather than transitioning to the nationally available ERIDS. The AAID application converts hard copy and paper data that is generated for government use to aid in air traffic operations. It is displayed in electronic format and made available at the control stations in addition to the paper copies of approach plates and orders. It also tracks equipment outages and active airspace that is used in active control of air traffic.

name: Safety Assurance System
description: The AFS Safety Assurance System (SAS) provides aviation safety inspectors (ASI) with standardized protocols and tools to evaluate certificate holder programs and safety performance. SAS implements FAA Safety Management System (SMS) policy within AFS by providing and assessing safety risk controls (i.e., regulations and their application) for aviation operators and individuals that fall within FAA regulations. SAS has been developed in accordance with FAA regulatory policy which recognizes the obligation of each certificate holder to maintain the highest possible degree of safety in the public interest. SAS directly supports the three primary FAA safety oversight responsibilities:• Verifying that an applicant can operate safety and comply with regulations and standards before issuing a certificate or approving/accepting programs;• Conducting periodic reviews to assure that a certificate holder continues to meet regulatory requirements when the environment changes; and,• Validating the performance of a certificate holder’s approved and accepted programs for the purpose of Continued Operational Safety (COS).

name: Knowledge Services Network
description:
The FAA's Knowledge Services Network (KSN) is an adaptable, integrated, shared community environment where individuals can manage content and processes, improve business insight, simplify internal/external collaboration and empower users to make a strategic impact.
KSN is a virtual workspace that supports a community of over 50,000 government staff employees, contractors, and partners (e.g. Airlines, other external businesses) who are using Microsoft Windows SharePoint Services to fundamentally alter the way knowledge work is done in their organizations.
KSN is a “Virtual Office Environment,” providing its users a web site that structures daily work into managed storage areas and categories such as document libraries, announcements, events, contacts, discussion boards, and miscellaneous lists. Within these areas, users can share and collaborate on their daily work. There are approximately 77,000 sites.
KSN is based on industry standard hardware and commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software. KSN consists of a family of tools that are fully Internet based and tightly integrated for delivering a collaborative knowledge-sharing environment. KSN provides access to users anywhere at any time as long as the user has an account and a connection to the Internet.

name: MyProfile
description:
MyProfile is the FAA's employee directory, providing contact information on all FA employees and contractors.

Data
The data in the system includes FAA contact information on employees, interns, contractors, and any other person granted access to the FAA network.  Maintaining an up-to-date profile in MyProfile is a requirement for FAA network access.  Additionally, the system maintains PII data related to a person beyond their relationship to the FAA.  This includes emergency contact, personal contact, and identity verification information.  Access to this data is restricted to those utilizing a least-privileged access policy.

Applications
The MyProfile system is composed of four applications that interact with the data: 
 - MyProfile web application: A web application, hosted on-prem, with an Oracle database.  Allows anyone on the FAA network to view public profile information and allows the same users to view and edit their own public and private data.
 - MyProfile Search:  A web application, hosted on-prem, allowing anyone on the FAA network to search the MyProfile directory.  Anyone on the FAA network may search the directory with links to view the records in the MyProfile web application.
 - MyProfile Admin: A set of reports and tools allowing MyProfile admins to ensure the health of the application and data.  Also allows designated users to track "capstone" officials for record retention compliance.
 - MyProfile Web services: A set of web APIs allowing machine-to-machine access to the MyProfile data.  The web services allow searching and viewing of profile data, data update capabilities, and data synchronization.  The web services are hosted and managed by the FAA API Center for Enablement (API C4E)

• SBS data (Data Type 1) - The data comes from publicly available websites via an HTTP Get. The site is checked every 15 minutes for a new almanac through an automated process.
• SSR and WAM (Data Type 2) - The database tables are directly updated by Compliance Monitor. The connection writes directly to the RAC at least once a day.

• Airspace data (Data Type 4) - The data comes from an FAA-controlled website via an HTTP Get. The site is checked every 24 hours through an automated process.
• Jamming and Interferences (Data Type 5) - The data comes from an FAA-controlled website via an HTTP Get. The site is checked every 24 hours through an automated process.

name: Identity Management System
description:
The IDMS provides services for the PIV Card request, identity proofing, verification, background investigation and validation of an applicant prior to PIV Card issuance. IDMS is an integral component of the FAA PIV process.  The primary mission of IDMS is to support the FAA PIV credentialing procedure that has been implemented by ASH, as mandated by Homeland Security Presidential Directive 12 (HSPD-12).
The IDMS system supports the issuance and/or maintenance of PIV cards for the Department of Transportation (DOT) Federal workforce; the DOT Contract workforce; members of the public, such as non-FAA employees who need access to FAA facilities, e.g., security guards and day care workers; approximately ten (10) Government Printing Office (GPO) employees; and approximately one thousand, five hundred (1500) Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) employees.
IDMS supports the technical, operational, and management requirements laid out by the Federal Information Processing Standard (FIPS) 201-1, which was developed in response to HSPD-12.  The IDMS architecture consists of web portals, database management systems, and interfaces that collectively perform various functions described in HSPD-12 and FIPS 201-1.  From a high level, the services supported by IDMS are:
PIV Card request Identity proofing Verification Background investigation validation of an applicant PIV Card issuance and maintenance. IDMS has two functional components, the Card Management System (CMS) and PIV Authoritative Database (PAD). The system references DOT SORN ALL 9 and NARA GRS 5.6.

name: Toxicology Database
description:
The Office of Aerospace Medicine (AAM) Civil Aerospace Medical Institute (CAMI) uses the Toxicology Database (TOXDB) system to enter and process information on individuals who have been involved in transportation accidents and incidents including, but not limited to, aviation, rail, bus, maritime, and trucking. TOXDB is an umbrella system that encompasses four separate applications: MANTRA, ICE, ToxFlo, and FileHold.

MANTRA (Medical Analysis Tracking) collect and secures data from fatal aviation accidents, ICE (Incident Collection and Examination) collects and secures data from nonfatal aviation accidents, ToxFlo is a laboratory information management system that runs the toxicology laboratory and creates toxicology reports, and FileHold is a secure document management system (FileHold) that stores files from toxicological analyses, aviation accidents, and also holds AAM-600 research and operational documents.

Data contained within the ToxDB system is used for continuing review and medical trend analysis by the AAM Safety Council.

name: ASH External Web Portal
description:
The ASH EWP is a collection of several internet-facing access points used to transfer data to and from specified internal FAA applications and databases.  These methods are available to approved and authenticated FAA vendors, FAA employees acting solely in an administrative capacity, non-FAA employees, and other federal agencies.  The ASH EWP system is located in a Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) area that is accessible from the internet. Nine (9) applications within the ASH EWP are currently operational:
Vendor Access Portal (VAP) – VAP enables FAA contractors to submit applications online for their employees to initiate FAA pre-employment investigations.
VAP Personnel Access Security System (PASS) – Application used to grant user and administrator accounts in the VAP system
International Visitor Program (IVP) – Web-based application that processes data from international visitors seeking approval to visit FAA facilities using FAA Form 1600.78. An FAA sponsor signs into https://destination.faa.gov or https://visitors.faa.gov and submits the initial request.  IVP then sends an email to the individual who is coordinating the site visit.  The email contains a secure link to the IVP web site that permits temporary access to submit visitor specific information.  The visitor POC accesses the IVP site through this link and enters the Form 1600.78 data online for the individuals who are applying for permission to visit.  The IVP application receives the data and immediately transfers it to an IVP database on the ASH Web Portal (which is in a separate Security Authorization domain wholly internal to the FAA).  The original data in the IVP database on the ASH EWP is purged.  Once on the ASH Web Portal, the data is then used by the FAA Office of International Affairs (API) to review the visit and forward it to AXF, ASH Service Area personnel, and the appropriate Line of Business (LOB) for review.  ASH Service Area personnel forward the visit to the appropriate FAA facility manager.
Secure File Transfer Protocol (SFTP) Service – Runs on an as needed basis to pull the data from Aviation Safety (AVS) - temporarily holds this data in a database in the ASH EWP (in encrypted form). After transfer, the data is purged from the ASH EWP database.
Security Awareness Virtual Initiative (SAVI) Course – Awareness tool that ASH uses to train employees and contractors on security requirements, measures, and safeguards to protect FAA assets. 
Personal Identity Verification (PIV) – Static web page used to show people where enrollment and bio pin reset stations are located.
ASH Classified National Security Information (CNSI) Course – All FAA employees, assigned military personnel, and contractors who hold security clearances must receive training on the basic principles and practices necessary to protect CNSI.  ASH developed a course, "Safeguarding Classified Information within the FAA," to meet the training requirements referenced in FAA Orders 1600.1E and 1600.2E. 
Customer Service (CS) Survey – Form accessed from a hyperlink that is appended to all ASH employee email signatures
The FAA Insider Threat Program and Reacting to an Active Shooter Event Course – Course offered to familiarize employees with the FAA Insider Threat and Active Shooter programs; which highlight if you “See Something, Say Something” and run, hide, fight.  This training course replicates the course that is offered through eLMS; the difference is that it is a public-facing site so that anyone who do not have access to the FAA intranet can still take the training.
In addition to these user-facing applications, one (1) other system component provides security services for the portal applications:
SiteMinder – A Computer Associates (CA) product, which provides centralized security policy management, authentication, and single sign-on for specified ASH EWP applications (at this time only VAP).

name: Instructional Resource Information System
description:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Academy’s, Instructional Resource Information System (IRIS), provides the FAA with the applications, programs, databases, and websites necessary to facilitate required training.  

IRIS contains operating systems, databases, applications, and support components used to automate the processes of the FAA Academy. In addition, IRIS contains many components which support other elements of the system. These include storage area networks (SAN), virtual hosting servers, backup devices and networking hardware.

Instructional Resource Information System (IRIS) started out in 1994 as a task to consolidate and automate several processes performed manually in the FAA Academy.  Original design of IRIS included a backend Oracle database that received training data from FAAs Consolidated Personnel Management Information System (CPMIS).  In addition, front-end applications were developed to simplify or automate existing academy processes.  These applications ranged from end of course/post course critiques, student services surveys, and  a welcome package generator to employees time and attendance records and labor activity data tracking system.  Approximately all 435 academy employees plus many contract personnel needed some kind of access to these applications.  Because each application had separate installation for every PC it would reside on, configuration control and maintenance became increasingly difficult to manage.

name: Investigations Tracking System
description:
Personnel Security Program (PSP) –  FAA processes a wide range of personnel security investigations through ITS. These investigations include current employees as well as those of potential applicants, contract employees and any other individuals (non-employees) with access to FAA facilities, systems, or information. The FAA uses ITS to record, track, adjudicate, and report on investigations pertaining to security background checks and clearances on employees, contractors and non-employees. 
• Internal Investigation Program (IIP) - ITS tracks investigations involving the following types of allegations: employee, contractor and non-employee misconduct, falsification of official documents, security violations, tort claims against the FAA, property theft.  The FAA uses ITS to record, track, and report on internal administrative investigations on cases relative to conduct and discipline matters.  
• Law Enforcement Assistance Program (LEAP) – ITS tracks investigations involving the following types of allegations: criminal activity by airmen and other FAA certificate holders, counterfeit certificates and other investigative services provided to law enforcement agencies.  ITS supports the FAA’s mandate to investigate the actual or probable violation by pilots, aircraft owners, or aircraft mechanics of civil and criminal laws regulating controlled substances. 
• Driving Under the Influence/Driving While Intoxicated (DUI/DWI) - ITS tracks investigations involving airmen that fail to notify the FAA when involved in alcohol related motor vehicle actions.  14 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 61.15 requires pilots to notify the FAA within 60 days of and alcohol and/or drug related conviction or administrative actions (motor vehicle actions (MVA)).

name: MyAccess
description:
The MyAccess program consists of five (5) services that support the Department of Transportation (DOT) and Federal Aviation Administration (FAA); MyAccess Workforce, Customer Identity and Access Management (CIAM), Identity Confidence Scoring, Hardware Security Modules (HSM) and DocuSign SaaS (to be rolled out in FY24). MyAccess Workforce provides 80,000 employees and contractors of the DOT and FAA the capability to log into an application using their personal identity verification (PIV)  card, thereby reducing the number of passwords an employee would be required to create, use, and recall for various applications. 

MyAccess CIAM enables the DOT and FAA to securely capture and manage customer identity and profile data, as well as control external (non-organizational) customer access to applications and services.

name: System of Airports Reporting
description:
The System of Airports Reporting (SOAR) is the primary mission support system supporting the FAA Office of Airports in administering and planning environmental and financial assistance programs and selected compliance functions.  SOAR currently supports four (4) program areas: (1)Airport Improvement Program (AIP) which tracks and reports grant projects at eligible airports and maintains grant fund accounts. (2) Air Carrier Activity Information System (ACAIS) which supports the Airport Improvement Program (AIP) by collecting and reporting enplanements and cargo landed weights and calculating AIP entitlement amounts. (3)Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) program which allows public agencies controlling public-use, commercial service airports to impose a fee on air travelers, and to use the funds on approved capital projects to improve on airport agency controls, and (4)National Plan of Integrated Airport Systems (NPIAS) which identifies existing and proposed airports that are eligible to receive AIP grants and compiles anticipated capital funding needs.
SOAR consists of two (2) major sub-systems: 1) SOAR Internal, which supports planning, environmental, grants, financial assistance, compliance, ACAIS, and PFC activities for the internal FAA users; and 2) Airports External Portal (AEP), previously named SOAR External, which supports PFC External functions and limited NPIAS and ACIP planning functions, accessible through the Internet to authorized airports and air carriers.

For the purposes of tracking in EAMS, System of Airports Reporting (SOAR) is SOAR Internal and Airports External Portal (AEP) is SOAR External,

name: AGIS - Life Cycle Asset Tracking System
fullname_0: AGIS - Life Cycle Asset Tracking System
description:
LCATS is a customized bar coding scanning software system which allow vendors and technicians to provide equipment information through a handheld device called the Automated Data Collection Tool (ADCT). ADCT currently has Wi-Fi disabled so technicians must load the ADCT data to their maintenance data terminals (MDTs) first and then upload to the LCATS database when network access is available. Asset information includes the vendor's production unit test report, shipment history, configuration, maintenance, and modification data.When surveyors are sent out to survey a facility in support of SSDB, they are encouraged, but not required, to scan equipment located in those facilities with ADCT. Currently, the focus of LCATS has been radio equipment, but Command Control Communications (C3), Power Services Group (PSG), and navigational aid (NAVAID) programs chose to utilize the AGIS capabilities for their asset tracking as well.The web-based interface facilitates the searching and reporting of equipment in the LCATS database based on a top-down identification hierarchy: program, service area, region, district, SSC, location, facility, vendor, equipment type, and serial number. Air Ground Information Systems (AGIS) has two sub-systems: 
-	SSDB: Site Survey Database
-	LCATS: LifeCycle Asset Tracking System

description: In the course of their duties, HR specialists are required to access DOT personnel records, such as the SF Form 50, Notification of Personnel Action, and SF Form 52, Request for Personnel Action, which are contained in FPPS Web Printing. Once an employee’s PII is available in FPPS Web Printing, it can be retrieved by searching for that individual’s name or social security number. HR specialists, system administrators, and technical database administrators have access to the PII contained in FPPS Web Printing. Web Printing uses logon names and passwords to control access and contains the name and password of the DOT users with access to the system. FPPSWeb Printing does not directly collect any information from any individuals. All information contained in FPPS Web Printing is retrieved from DOI’s FPPS database. HR specialists require this information for the performance of their duties. This information is retrieved from DOI’s FPPS so that HR specialists do not have to duplicate a Federal Government information collection system.

name: FAA Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation
description:
The Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation (CDM) system is a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) system designed to support the organization’s continuous monitoring strategy by providing centralized inventory management and control, scanning and patching capabilities, and device monitoring and reporting. The CDM system will provide senior Agency officials with an enterprise level view of the security posture of FAA information technology (IT) assets.  The CDM system servers are hosted at the Office of Information & Technology Enterprise Data Center at the William J. Hughes Technical Center (AIT EDC (WJHTC)). Certain CDM system components are also expected to be present at local, regional, and national FAA facilities.
The Federal Aviation Administration Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation (FAA CDM) system is an FAA set of tools designed to support the organization’s continuous monitoring strategy by providing centralized inventory management and control, scanning and patching capabilities, and device monitoring and reporting. The CDM system will provide senior Agency officials with an enterprise level view of the security posture of FAA information technology (IT) assets.
The FAA implemented the FAA CDM system as part of the FAA Information Security Continuous Monitoring (ISCM) strategy. CDM enables senior officials within the FAA to get a high-level view of the security state of the FAA and its information systems. Senior officials and their staffs are able to acquire near real-time visibility throughout the FAA infrastructure to support well-informed decisions and prioritize risk mitigation activities. The FAA provides object-level detailed information to DOT and summary level data to DHS CISA via the Department’s CDM Dashboard.
FAA-CDM components are currently deployed into the Mission Support and Research & Development (R&D) operating environments.
The system is currently comprised of twelve (12) components:
• ForeScout CounterACT: Security tool that dynamically identifies and evaluates network devices and applications as they connect to the FAA network. The ForeScout CounterACT appliances hosted in the Research & Development (R&D) environment are a part of the FAA CDM Authorization Boundary. The ForeScout CounterACT appliances hosted in the Mission Support environment are managed by AIT Networks and are outside of the FAA CDM authorization boundary.
• Tenable Security Center: The FAA Security Operations Center (SOC) and the Enterprise Service Center (ESC) operate separate instances of Tenable Security Center, also referred to as Nessus. Both Tenable instances are outside of the FAA CDM authorization boundary.
• HCL BigFix: Policy enforcement tool that discovers all endpoints, scans all endpoints, and can apply missing patches. BigFix is used for update (patching) services and reporting services (reporting configuration settings and software assets) and running on all managed endpoints in the Research & Development domain. Though it is outside of the authorization boundary, Directory Services BigFix sends CDM reporting data to CDM Splunk.

description:
The FAADroneZone is a cloud-based IT platform that hosts several applications and the supporting infrastructure that improves the user experience of public interactions and increases efficiency of internal business processes. The Initial Operating Capability (IOC) of the FAADroneZone went into production on January 6th, 2018.  The initial release included the platform, the sUAS Registration Service and the collection and processing of Airspace Authorizations and Waivers, Operational Waivers and Accident Reporting under Part 107.   In addition, the FAADroneZone platform also supports the backend IT systems that runs the LAANC program.  
When a new requirement is identified, the FAADroneZone will provide the platform of IT services because the FAADroneZone platform was built using modern cloud-based tools, services and development practices. Data generated from these sUAS processes are also stored on a central cloud-based database that allows for more effective and efficient use of the data in support of activities such as risk-based decision-making, economic forecasting and trend analysis.

description: The FAA SOC includes CSMC Intrusion Prevention Systems.  It was established to monitor the FAA and DOT cyber security environments and to actively combat and prevent cyber-based attacks. The FAA SOC is a focal point for information security incident monitoring and response, intrusion detection sensor data analysis, forensic activities, vulnerability scanning, and provides both the FAA and DOT assistance with cyber disaster recovery and responsive corrective actions.  The FAA SOC is moving from a reactive to a proactive organization which will leverage threat intelligence to hunt for and thwart adversaries.  The CSMC mission is to protect the FAA and DOT information systems infrastructure, prevent unauthorized access, detect hostile acts, respond to attacks, and recover from malicious degradation. The mission is also to provide a shared service provider level of services to other Federal agencies seeking to protect their critical information system infrastructure and network operations from compromise, disruption, or termination resulting from exploitation of their information systems.

IFPA provides the ability to input aeronautical data used in the development, flight check and maintenance of flight procedures.  The system incorporates data from a multitude of sources using a Service Oriented Architecture (SOA), enabling the concept of data stewardship and provides the capability to deliver aeronautical data associated with procedures to the FAA Enterprise. This system is designed to supply data in time slices for past, present, and future flight-procedure operations throughout the FAA.  This data can be used by other organizations using the Aeronautical Information Exchange Message (AIXM). This includes support for the QJLauncher, as it is an incorporated portion of the Quintiq 2020 software. CyTF provides an independent and adaptable research and development environment to conduct cybersecurity test and evaluation activities for the National Airspace System (NAS), as it evolves to the Next Generation Air Transportation System (NextGen). CyTF supports the following test and evaluation capabilities for the NAS:
• Identification and validation of cybersecurity threats 
• Integration of new cybersecurity capabilities, tools and technologies 
• Transition to a continuous monitoring of the information system environment 
• Improve processes to respond and recover from cybersecurity events
• Assess and improve current resilience capabilities

description:
Supports full lifecycle management activities for telecommunication services and facilities. The TEMT Suite supports the management of telecommunications services and facilities through the entire life cycle by integrating the telecommunications engineering and operations capabilities under one system that improves efficiency, data sharing and data integration/consistency. The TEMT Suite is made up of the following component applications:

The Quality Performance Management System (QPMS) serves as a tool for managing the data entry, analysis, and reporting of performance data for the FAA CONUS Flight Service Quality Assurance (QA) process. The QPMS acts as a central repository of performance information. The QPMS provides FAA management with up-to-date performance information, and generates reports and trend analysis for the QA team. The system consists of a Microsoft Access front-end application for data input, a read only website, and a SQL Server database. Data is entered into the Microsoft Access application (online or offline) and then uploaded to the Microsoft Windows SQL Server database when the user is online. The website provides a read only interface to the data stored within the SQL Server database.

name: AIR Work Tracking System Tools
description:
AIR WTS is composed of modules that facilitate data input used in the FAA AIR Certification and Authorization Process.  The data is used to track and manage various work activities e.g., (Suspense Tracking, Correspondence Tracking, AD-HOC Task Management, Continued Operational Safety, Issue Paper Development, Reports and Metrics, Import Tools, Administrator Tools, and Help).
The data entered for AIR WTS includes Transactional Data, Milestone and Disposition Data, and other data to support risk-based decision-making for several organizational efforts. This data includes but is not limited to:
•	Correspondence Management: incoming and outgoing correspondence received from and transmitted to stakeholders, correspondence category, date received and transmitted, and disposition.
•	Aircraft Certification Projects (augments data collected in a separate application): risk-based decision data, project prioritization, and milestones.
•	Aircraft Safety Events (augments data collected in a separate application): safety decision information received from Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), milestones, and disposition.
•	Issue Paper Development: nature of Issue Paper, milestones, disposition, and supporting data.

As of July 2022, AIR WTS was deployed using a .net custom user interface instead of the COTS interface MS Access. The processes, functions and abilities for the web version remain the same as for the COTS version. For distinction between the two versions, AIR WTS 1.0 is the COTS (MS Access) version and AIR WTS 2.0 is the web, (MS .net) version.

name: Physical Security Enterprise Management System
description:
The PSEMS system consists of four subsystems:  a Physical Security Information Management Subsystem (PSIMS), a Cardholder Information Access Distribution Subsystem (CIADS), a Physical Access Control System (PACS), and an On-Demand Video Subsystem (ODVS).  Together these subsystems provide the capability to remotely monitor and respond to facility physical access control alarms.  Additionally, these subsystems establish connectivity between a facility PACS and the FAA PAD (PIV Access Directory).

The PSEMS system allows security personnel the ability to monitor and respond to facility security alarms at Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) facilities when security guards are either not located on site or the security guards are occupied with other required duties. The system coordinates the transfer of current cardholder information associated with FAA issued badges to all connected facilities.  This allows security personnel to notify all facilities when granting or revoking personnel access at FAA facilities.

name: Just In Time Training
description:
To provide ASI and other Flight Standard employee’s training resources in the form of Just in Time Training (JIT). The JIT format used focuses on making learning content immediately and readily available so that Inspectors can learn under their own direction and motivation. Key points of a course are captured to assist Inspectors in successfully completing their job tasks. The just-in-time model is characterized by three things:
1. Self-direction: The learner controls what is learned, and in what order.
2. This type of learning is location and time-independent: Learners can access information and tools of learning virtually, anywhere and at any time. JITs are designed so they can be accessed from the field in multiple ways including from a laptop, tablet, or phone
3. Learning in this model has a key functional aspect: Recall what was previously taught and to use the JIT information to assist the learner in his/her immediate job task.

JIT training can come in the form of PDF’s, short videos, graphics, excel, and a few web pages. We are trying to build a JIT training portal for AFS divisions.

name: Aerobytes - Flight Operational Quality Assurance
description:
Flight Data Monitoring (FDM) and Flight Operations Quality Assurance (FOQA) program that allows continuous improvement and corrective actions that can be assessed by overlaying them on performance graphs. Aircraft is being measured and how it is flown. Statistics (including trend flight data to find developing trends) then drive a continuous improvement process (Aerobytes Ltd, 2014).
Processes flight data from FAA Flight Program aircraft for safety analysis in support of AJF's FAA-Approved Flight Operational Quality Assurnace (FOQA) Program.

Recorded flight data from each aircraft is processed by the software which then identifies areas of concern (in respect of pilot-handling, operational procedures or maintenance issues).

Data and information from FOQA programs are protected from disclosure in accordance with 14 CFR part 193. Therefore, data from this program is shared only within Flight Program Operations and the specific Flight Standards office that is responsible for oversight and surveillance. It may not be shared with other offices within the FAA.

name: Federal NOTAM System
description:
Federal NOTAM System (FNS) is the modernized Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) management system designed to digitize the collection, dissemination, and storage of NOTAMs.  The goal is to create a single authoritative source for NOTAM entry and dissemination to improve the efficiency, safety, and data quality of NOTAM information.

Within the modernized NOTAM concept of operations, the entire NOTAM process has been re-engineered to support improved NOTAM origination, management, and distribution. The basic concept behind FNS is to have the NOTAM originator generate and submit the NOTAM using a web-based standard template. The inputs from the standard template will be validated against policy-driven business rules and immediately published. The NOTAM information will also ultimately be distributed in digital format to external users.
The FNS consists of an ecosystem of services and applications that, together, bring this modernized NOTAM concept to life.

name: UAS Services
description:
Remote identification of Unmanned Aircraft Systems (UAS) is necessary to address aviation safety and security issues related to the integration and operation of UAS in the National Airspace System and is an essential component of future UAS Traffic Management. National security partners, Federal, State, and local law enforcement agencies need to know the location and identity of unmanned aircraft (UA) and must be able to locate the control station. For security reasons and threat discrimination purposes, they also need to have near real-time access to remote ID messages.
UAS Services configuration would allow third-party service suppliers qualified by the FAA to offer remote ID services. The project scope will include design, development and integration of services to facilitate the processing of remote ID messages data and for law enforcement to attain flight and pilot information for investigative purposes.
The DISCVR UI provides a streamlined ability for authorized consumers to query the FAADroneZone and LAANC read database replicas via the DISCVR API as necessary for program operation, analysis, and planning objectives. Users can search on Registration Number, Serial Number, or timestamp. There is also a user administration component to DISCVR UI that allows for adding users to a DISCVR UI authentication table.

name: ATC Facilities Toolkit
description: ATC Facilities Toolkit (ATC FacT) is a system containing various sub systems that provides access to FAA Facilities data and its system and sub component level data in support of the NAS. This information includes, but is not limited to, physical dimensions of equipment, building information, general terminal information, location of equipment, service area equipment, and configuration management audit data.  By housing all of this information in one central repository (ATC FacT), FAA employees will be able to, in real-time, pull accurate and trustworthy data as opposed to waiting on time-consuming information requests or relying on outdated resources.  The data contained in the sub systems of ATC FacT can also be analyzed to support focused decision making for their intended target areas.

name: Enterprise Information Display System
description: E-IDS is part of the FAA’s efforts to increase NAS safety and efficiency by providing modernized and streamlined technology to its workforce. The enterprise-level platform and display will provide controllers with a tailorable, robust data navigation design and enable intuitive access to operationally significant information, including dynamic weather data, notices to airmen and pilot reports. It accomplishes this through a centralized, cloud-ready architecture that leverages FAA investments in NAS enterprise infrastructure and services, including improvements in static data aggregation and management processes.

5/13/2025 - Per review by ATO Security and Elizabeth.T-CTR.Phan:  FY25 package pending eSign entry for signature process.

5/8/2024 - Per meeting with Bruce Dennis, this is in progress in SMART| Per FAA Daily Broadcast on 10/16/2024 - A new display system gives air traffic controllers easy access to information necessary to manage aircraft safely and efficiently. Enterprise Information Display Systems (E-IDS) provide position-focused Notices to Air Missions (NOTAM) to each controller position and prompt controllers to solicit Pilot Reports (PIREP) based on current weather conditions. The resulting PIREP will be distributed throughout the E-IDS system and to the Submit PIREP service. These E-IDS features address two of the Air Traffic Organization’s (ATO) Top Five Safety Issues for accurate and efficient solicitation and dissemination of air traffic information with PIREPs and NOTAMs. “It was a concerted effort, drawing on lessons learned from past projects and integrating them into our planning for E-IDS,” said Roger Desir, a general engineer and representative of Engineering Services. E-IDS completed its first key site survey at Atlantic City International Airport (ACY) in May, followed by the National Enterprise Management Centers (NEMC) in Atlanta and Salt Lake City in June. The strategic choice of ACY as the first key site survey highlights the project’s commitment to leveraging existing infrastructure and expertise to optimize the deployment process. Looking ahead, the teams will monitor and evaluate E-IDS performance post-deployment at ACY, leveraging the capabilities of the NEMCs. This ongoing evaluation will ensure the system meets operational needs and evolves in response to emerging requirements. “The ability to monitor and evaluate the system at an enterprise level ensures that we can continue to refine and enhance E-IDS to meet the evolving needs of air traffic management,” Desir said.

name: FAA Cloud Services Amazon Web Services East/West
fullname_0: FAA Cloud Services Amazon Web Services East/West
description:
The Federal Aviation Administration Cloud Services Amazon Web Services (FCS AWS) Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) is a Public cloud service offering (CSO) provided by the Amazon Web Services (AWS) East/West Public Cloud. The Customer Controls are identified in the FedRAMP required Control Implementation Summary (CIS) submitted by Amazon as part of the required FedRAMP documentation. It defines the customer (FAA) responsibilities required to support FAA applications hosted in the AWS IaaS environment. 
The FCS AWS CSO is intended to meet the FAA’s business and technology mission to offer cloud-computing technology to System Owners for their applications or as an alternative to traditional data-center-hosted, legacy applications. Cloud computing provides the FAA and System Owners an opportunity to increase cost efficiency, accelerate delivery of services, and increase information sharing while supporting innovation, research and development, and sustainability.
AWS is a multi-tenant, public cloud that provides Federal, State, and local Government customers, as well as commercial customers, with cloud services.  AWS is designed to meet a wide range of regulatory requirements including government compliance and security requirements. AWS implements and provides an Infrastructure-as-a-Service (IaaS) cloud-computing model that enables convenient, on-demand Internet access to a shared pool of configurable computing resources such as servers, storage devices, network infrastructure, and web services. Customers can provision or release computing resources on demand.  AWS manages physical and logical access controls for the AWS infrastructure. The FAA is responsible for controlling user access to hosted applications and associated FAA data within the FAA’s FCS AWS.

name: Development Security Operations Support Tools
description:
“DevOps is a methodology and approach that pulls together developers, operations personnel and other IT professionals to automate and optimize the delivery of applications and infrastructure. It establishes common tools and languages for building, testing, and deploying software and configuration changes. It promotes collaboration and information sharing which enables solutions to be delivered more rapidly, with higher quality and increased security. DevOps is a key capability for fully realizing AIT’s movement towards Agile software development and migrating to the Cloud.” (Holiday, 2017)
DevSecOps is the product of the integration of security into the phases of DevOps. This process holds the participants in the systems development life cycle (SDLC) accountable for their role in securing the application. DevSecOps Support Tools provides FAA with the capability to provide automated security services within each phase of the SDLC. For example, when writing programs in the development factory, the programmers can use SonarQube to scan the source code for vulnerabilities. Tools such as Jenkins can build security into the continuous integration/continuous delivery (CI/CD) process. Developers can use OWASP Zed Application Proxy (ZAP) to scan for weaknesses during the testing phase. Other tools such as Jira track the progress of security issues from detection to resolution.

description:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is committed to providing the safest, most efficient aerospace system in the world.  In order to support this mission, the FAA Hotline and Whistleblower Information System (FHWIS), provides the ability for the public and FAA employees/contractors to report concerns regarding the safety of the National Airspace System, violation of a Federal Aviation Regulation (Title 14 CFR), aviation safety issues, and reports related to FAA employees or FAA facilities. 
FHWIS submissions are made through a web interface that redirects the reports to various offices within FAA.  Once a report is received, case intake analysts review forward to the appropriate office for investigation.  The FHWIS system that tracks the reports is hosted in the Salesforce Government Cloud Plus (FedRAMP ID FR2003061248).  FHWIS is utilizing the Salesforce Customer Relationship Management (CRM) Software-as-a-Service (SaaS) pieces that include Service Cloud CRM, Lightning Platform, and Digital Experience Cloud. FHWIS is a shared system with AAE and FS.  The “Case” module supports AEE, and the investigative module supports FS. FS handles all hotline and whistleblower assignments, investigations, and approvals and AAE is the sponsor for the project.  The O&M funding and yearly ATO security asst cost was split between AAE and FS, and each pay for their own licenses, development, and enhancements.

description:
FAA must ensure that systems using the 1030/1090 MHz spectrum band can operate safely and are compatible within the National Airspace System (NAS). The U.S. Department of Defense, Office of the Chief Information Officer (DOD CIO) has tasked FAA with developing an automated tool to assess whether new systems are compatible with the existing and future 1030/1090 MHz environment. This effort results in the Cooperative Surveillance and 1030/1090 MHz Spectrum Environment Model (CSSEM), which will be used by the FAA Spectrum Engineering Office, DOD stakeholders, equipment manufacturers, and other stakeholders in cooperative surveillance and 1030/1090 MHz spectrum within the U.S. & Possessions (US&P).

This system resides under the Federal aviation Administration (FAA) NextGen (ANG)/Surveillance Branch (C33). The system is owned and managed by FAA. The system utilizes web-based forms, produces reports, and contains interconnections/data exchanges with FAA and non-FAA systems. The system will be developed at the FAA William J. Hughes Technical Center in Atlantic City, NJ; this is also the main site of the system, there are no support sites. CSSEM plans to utilize FAA Cloud Services.

name: AVS Safety Reporting Program
description:
Voluntary safety reporting is a critical element of a successful Safety Management System (SMS). FAA encourages the adoption of SMS and voluntary safety reporting in the aviation industry and recognizes the value in these programs as contributing to a healthy and positive safety culture. AVS recognizes the need to hold ourselves accountable to the same best practices we encourage externally.

The AVS VSRP is modeled after the successful Aviation Safety Action Programs (ASAP) used in the aviation industry. ASAP can be traced back to the early 1970s and a voluntary safety reporting program at United Airlines. More recent examples are the Voluntary Safety Reporting Program for Air Traffic Controllers (ATSAP) and the Voluntary Safety Reporting Program for Technicians (T-SAP). These and other programs depend on employee input to identify significant safety concerns and issues, operational deficiencies, non-compliance with regulations, deviations from company policies and procedures, and unusual safety events. In partnership with each participating aviation organization, employee labor organizations, and the FAA, each ASAP report is investigated and corrective actions determined based on a non-disciplinary approach to improving safety.

fullname_0: AFN AIT Proofpoint Federal Production Environment SaaS
description:
The Proofpoint Federal Production Environment provides a complete message archiving solution that can protect an organization from legal liabilities and regulatory risks while improving E-mail storage management and end-user productivity. It contains emails from 2013 till Oct. 31st, 2022.  Its web interface offers E-mail archiving with robust search and discovery, supervision, and enforcement features.  The solution stores electronic messages for a specified retention period, while keeping the messages fully searchable and retrievable in real-time or using a batch process.  This allows archived messages to be easily viewed, retrieved to a user’s E-mail inbox or exported to an Outlook data file.

The Archiving Appliance is a sealed fixed-purpose server that is installed within a Proofpoint Customer’s network behind the firewall, to provide the integration and security traditionally found in internally hosted systems.  The appliance integrates with Microsoft Exchange to ensure reliable, native format message archiving.  Its integration with Active Directory facilitates unified login and access control management.  Since the appliance is the only holder of the encryption keys used with the Proofpoint DoubleBlind™ Encryption technology, any processing that involves encryption or decryption happens on the appliance.

plannedactivitiesdescription_0:
Proofpoint versions are a bit different.  Here is the explanation: I checked with Proofpoint Support regarding the version that displays on their appliances after an upgrade and they indicates that the appliances always display “3.x” in front of the upgrade. Therefore, if the Proofpoint appliances are to be upgraded from version 5.0.001 to 5.1.002, when you do the verification after an upgrade it display with the 3. first and we would see it as version 3.5.1.002. 

Therefore, I do not believe it is necessary to submit a request to the ESB on our behalf to have version 5.x added and reviewed. It is just that the Proofpoint appliance display/ interpret the upgrade version by appending the number “3.” at the beginning of the version. If necessary, I can get a statement from Proofpoint Operations to collaborate this statement. The next update will take place in Jan/Feb 2024. 
| 1/15/2025 - Per POC: The intention is to discontinue Proofpoint, however there are a few dependencies. The main one being that Records Management Office (RMO) needs to start notifying LoBs/SO and users that emails older than 7 years will be permanently deleted for regular users and 25 years for those designated as capstone users to comply with NARA approved retention schedule for FAA. A plan will be developed after reviewing the RMO communications plan.

Per Shalini Jerath during AIT Lunch & Learn on 11/13/2023 - Proofpoint will soon be discontinued as the ability for Email Archiving has been implemented in M365

name: Physical Security Enterprise Management System 2
description: PSEMS2 system consists of three integrated, enterprise capable subsystems: Cardholder Information Access Distribution Subsystem (CIADS2), a Physical Access Control Subsystem (PACS2), an On-Demand Video Subsystem (ODVS2). The PACS is Lenel Onguard software and Lenel controller boards.  It monitors physical security components such as electronic door strikes, badge and PIN code readers, motion sensors, and door position sensors.The ODVS is Genetec Security Center software, it manages real-time and recorded viewing and control of local CCTV cameras. The CIADS is TI EntryPoint software that is capable of local and enterprise level provisioning of cardholders with an established connectivity between the PACS and FAA PAD (PIV Access Directory).

name: SWIM Cloud Distribution System
description:
GDIT Infrastructure as a Service for SWIM Cloud Distribution Service                      
The SWIM program is a National Airspace System (NAS)-wide information system that supports Next Generation Air Transportation System (NextGen) goals. SWIM facilitates the data sharing requirements for NextGen, providing the digital data-sharing backbone of NextGen. This information-sharing platform offers a single point of access for aviation data, with producers of data publishing it once and users accessing the information they need through a single connection. Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) is designing the solution for these external data consumers to reduce costs and resources and to improve the user experience.  
The FAA uses an alternative approach for providing SWIM data to external users which is more efficient and cost effective. The FAA uses Cloud Services (FCS), an Amazon Web Services (AWS)-hosted IaaS, supported by GDIT, a third-party service provider.  
Configuration of the AWS account uses external environments completely outside the FAA or FCS for hosting, utilizing AWS Public Internet Protocol (IP) addresses and public services. The resources hosted within this SCDS AWS account transverse the FAA Trusted Internet Connection (TIC) to reach anything within the FAA.
