name: Visual Support Network
description: DTIS will provide Software as a Service (SaaS) as a software distribution model in which a cloud provider hosts applications and makes them available to end users over the internet. The software delivery model uses a provider to host the customer's software and delivers it to approved end users from the FAA Mission Support (MS) Network. The Visual Support Network (VSN) tool uses electronic processing from multiple sensors to capture data of a physical NAS facility. VSN transforms the electronic data, captured from the facility into a data aggregated model of the facility. VSN processes data within the model allowing the user to utilize the data for presentational suggestions both remotely and locally. The VSN tool essentially involves capturing data of FAA facilities and equipment. The result is referred to as a "digital twin" of the chosen facility. DTIS LLC will capture, aggregate, and then move the data (VSN Processed Data and Raw Data) from the capture devices (on a secure and encrypted removal drive) to the FCS production subnet ("S3" bucket, VMs, and Database) for use by authenticated and authorized FAA "clients". The authorized clients would potentially include Engineering Services, Program Management Office (PMO), Tech Ops, and Second-Level Engineering (SLE).

name: U.S. Agent for Service Portal
description: Currently, serving documents to individuals across the world who hold and/or apply for FAA-issued certificates presents a challenge for the FAA. Accomplishing valid service abroad of certain FAA documents requires compliance with international service requirements under multi-lateral treaties. As a result, this rulemaking proposes adding a new subpart C to title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (14 CFR). The proposed subpart C requires individuals who hold or apply for certificates issued under 14 CFR parts 47, 61, 63, 65, 67, or 107 and who do not have a U.S. physical address of record on file with the FAA to designate a U.S. agent. The U.S. agent would receive service of FAA documents on behalf of the applicant or certificate holder.

name: Regional Information System
description: REGIS is the FAA official financial cuff record system for OPS, F&E, ACT5, and Airport Administrative funds that allows users to allocate, record, manage, report and reconcile financial transactions against Delphi, the official Agency accounting system. REGIS also includes the capability to build and manage spend plans. REGIS provides functionality across key areas such as Financial Management, Personnel, Administration and Budget Formulation and Execution.REGIS is designed to provide accurate, standardized and timely financial tracking across an entire organization. REGIS consists of 5 modules: Transactions, Reports, Allocations, Spend Plan, and Administration. Some of the capabilities of REGIS include: • Allocate, record transactions, and reconcile OPS, F&E Activity 5, and Airports Administrative accounts funding• Allocate down and roll up funding at every organizational level• Automatically reconcile financial transactions against Delphi expenditures. Note: REGIS also has Delphi obligations - users can manually reconcile obligation data• Filter, Analyze, and Export Data• Build, track, and report on Spend Plan• Use dynamic filtering for onscreen reports (REGIS has over 100 preformatted reports)• Use ad hoc reporting capabilities to Export data to Excel.

name: Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application
fullname_0: Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application
description: The Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application (IACRA) is a web-based program that automates the airman certification and rating application process. The system is accessible over the Internet and integrates multiple FAA national databases to validate data and verify specific fields in IACRA. The IACRA process provides the following benefits to all users:• Assigns FAA Tracking Numbers (FTN) to all registered users• Provides immediate validation checks of information entered on applications to help reduce errors and validate certain data• Provides a means to electronically submit certification applications to the Airmen Certification Branch• Provides the ability to sign applications via electronic screen capture, allowing the certification process to function in a paperless environment as mandated by the Government Paperwork Elimination Act (GPEA). Approximately 65% of users submit applications electronically.• Provides continuous access to the latest web-based version of IACRA for registered users

name: National Offload Program
description:
The National Offload Program (NOP) is a system of hardware and software located in each Standard Terminal Automation Replacement System (STARS), Micro EARTS (MEARTS) facilities, and center air traffic facility throughout the country for the primary purpose of providing real-time and archived data via the FAA Intranet concerning the location and movement of aircraft flying within the United States National Airspace System (NAS). FAA authorized users access the data for the purposes of: Operational error detection, Airspace utilization and efficiency reports and studies, Traffic count, Air traffic controller training and Administrative tracking of time on position (Note: NOP only processes raw data utilized by downstream applications that create metadata in support of the above described initiatives).  
NOP information is used within downstream FAA systems by Air Traffic Managers in the field for analysis of their airspace sector. The systems using the NOP information include FAA Headquarters personnel for statistical analysis of air traffic, local airport personnel for noise abatement and a myriad of other FAA organizations. This data is used to provide statistics related to flight plans, target tracks, and the business aspect of air traffic, which includes cost accounting, work productivity, traffic counts, resource management, etc.

description: MedXPress is an external application available on the Internet at https://medxpress.faa.gov/. Users self-register for a user account and are sent a confirmation email with their account information, including an initial password or PIN. Users are required to change their password after initial login. All persons requesting an FAA medical certificate or medical clearance are required to submit FAA Form 8500-8 electronically through MedXPress.

Per Bill Lampiris on 8/8/2023, ODT data resides in the Documentum platform located in Silver Springs.  That Documentum platform is used by AJV for Aeronautical charting data and is managed and supported by ADE-500 not ADE-300 (legacy Karyl Cooper). Now, ODT data as you both know has a front-end application called OEAAA and that application is managed and supported by AJV. 

As far as I know ADE is not involved in the support of that application. The plans are to move ODT data from the Silver Springs Documentum into FAA-EDMS (Alfresco) and when that happens ADE-300 will be responsible for the Alfresco platform while AJV continues to manage the application.| 10/31/2024; 11/7/2024 - Mary (APM) emailed Kattie Venticinque and asked if she had any information on the migration of the ASN Cabinet to Alfresco. 

10/1/2024 - Per Ashley Sherrod, the new date is 10/31/2024 for the Alfresco upgrade. The Alfresco update was delayed due to unanticipated Production issues we’ve experienced, which took precedence over Alfresco 7.x upgrade activities over the last several weeks.  Since then, we have resolved those Production issues and currently have not seen any additional issues regarding disk space and storage on the FAA- EDMS platform 

9/10/2024-Per Ashley Sherrod, the Alfresco upgrade to 7.x is still in progress. They are targeting an estimated completion date of 9/30.

8/20/2024 - Samba Chanamolu stated that Katie Venticinque from the business can update APM with her data migration efforts to Alfresco. Bill Lampiris said to add Ashley Sherrod and Timothy Naylor as the technical contacts.

5/7/2024 - Per Brian Murphy, the Obstacle Data Team’s use of the legacy Documentum system, have been migrated to Alfresco Share. The remaining artifacts supporting the Obstruction Evaluation Group (OEG) is in the works and migration efforts are underway. Reiterated by Samba Chanamolu, only one big content chunk (OEG/ASN) is still residing on current Documentum application software/hardware components. Once that migration activity is completed, they can recycle current hardware and software components.

5/7/2024 - APM sent the technical contacts, including Angela Edmonds, requesting their updated technology plans or status.
On 11/21-22/2023, Bill Lampiris replied stating that the Documentum cabinets are ODT and ASN.  ODT has been moved and the OE-AAA application has been changed to support EDMS.  The same will happen with the ASN cabinet by the end of this year 2023.  So, once ASN is moved to EDMS and the application changes move to production the entire ODT data sets (cabinets) would have been moved. ODT is no longer using Documentum however ASN is.  Once ASN moves to EDMS then the entire Documentum instance in support of AJV would be sunset remediating RHEL 6 and Microsoft IE Compatibility Mode within MS Edge items.

•	ODT cabinet is planned to move to EDMS September 2023
•	ASN cabinet is very large and planned to move to EDMS during November - December 2023

On 4/11/2023, Bill Lampiris stated that there are major issues with Alfresco have put on hold all the transitions from Documentum to Alfresco. We do not have an ETA. Once the production issues are resolved we will continue the migration which would take about 1 – 2  months.
As per Bill Lampiris on 1/9/2023, all the items (EOL and near EOL technologies) in red will remain as they are until the data and applications are moved to FAA EDMS (Alfresco).  We are hoping to have moved everything off Documentum  and into Alfresco by the end of March.  At that point we will sunset the Documentum instance.

description: The Traffic Count Index Program (TCIP) is a web-based collection utility that replaced the Terminal Track Analysis Program (TTAP) in October 2012. The primary function of TCIP is to collect and collate traffic counts from Terminal air traffic facilities and calculate a facility Traffic Count Index (TCI). Aircraft operations are entered in Count Ops via manual or automated means, by hour, into categories used under the complexity formula (for pay settings) to establish a facility’s pay level. TCIP provides a web-based front-end interface accessible via the ATO Application Portal (AAP) which interfaces with Count Ops for traffic count data, calculates the Traffic Count Index (TCI), provides facilities with a vehicle to monitor and request profile changes, provides facilities with a vehicle to upload traffic count validations, provides tools for the National Validation Team (NVT) to monitor and verify the accuracy of the TCI, and generates reports

name: Real Estate Management System
description: REMS is a web-based PIV-enabled system that tracks approximately 27,000 real property assets that includes approximately $6.2 Billion value of properties, 112 thousand acres of land and 26 million square foot of buildings. The data is used in responding to requirements for Executive Order 13327 and GSA FRPC Guidance for the entire DOT. OMB mandates the reporting of inventory, identification of disposals and Federal Sustainable Buildings. The primary goal of the real property initiative is to eliminate excess real property assets from the federal inventory.  Assets that are surplus, are not mission critical, are in poor condition, are under-utilized, and/or reflect high annual operation and maintenance costs should be considered candidates for disposition. Real property data is also used to support internal FAA analyses of space consolidation across LOBs.  REMS is comprised of virtualized web, application, and database servers in production and preproduction with a Team Foundation Server.  REMS servers are virtualized and hosted in the Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center (MMAC).  REMS is managed by Aviation Property Management (APM-200) in Washington DC Headquarters.

name: Document Imaging Workflow System
description: DIWS is a web-based internal application used by CAMI, OAM personnel at CAMI, FAA employees in regional offices, and employees at FAA Headquarters (HQ). DIWS effectively manages information regarding the medical certification of airmen. The primary goal of DIWS is to provide electronic file management of the hundreds of thousands of airman medical certification applications that are received and processed on an annual basis by CAMI. The DIWS software system automates many sections of the certification business process. As part of the automation process, all pilot and ATCS correspondence is stored electronically to allow real-time sharing of applicant records throughout the AAM Certification Division. All documentation sent to AAM from the pilot is electronically captured as digital images and imported into the applicant’s record. These documents are manually scanned and indexed by the medical certification division personnel at CAMI or by personnel in one of the regional offices. The documents are indexed or named according to the type of document. These names (or document types) are used in the automation process as well as visually by AAM personnel to identify critical information and relevance to the applicant’s medical certification application. DIWS incorporates a workflow application that allows OAM personnel, specifically AAM-300 personnel, to track each FAA Form 8500-8 medical certification application. Workflow also supports the review of the cases of applicants. DIWS maintains historical data and performs validation checks on new airman medical certification applications against previous exams.

description: Instrument Flight Procedures (IFP) SIAP is the tool for documenting approach data associated with instrument flight procedure development. This tool is intended to replace the current manual process in which SIAP information is documented and distributed.  This tool, as part of the Instrument Flight Procedure Automation (IFPA) suite of applications, will ensure that IFP SIAP information is documented in accordance with current published criteria, properly versioned, maintained in alignment with supporting aeronautical data for the estimated chart cycle, and guarantee only authorized personnel can modify the data at the appropriate steps in the IFP lifecycle.  The IFP SIAP tool will also enable the IFP SIAP data to be discoverable and exchanged in an industry recognized format, achieving the organizational goal of providing aeronautical information as a service.

name: FAA Federal Human Resources Navigator
description:
The FAA FedHR Navigator (FAA-FHR) is a Software as a Service (SaaS) enterprise application available by subscription to Federal agencies.  This SaaS has a Joint Authorization Board – Provisional (JAB-P) Authorization to Operate (ATO) that was granted in May 2014, as documented in the FedRAMP Economic Systems Inc., FedHR Navigator (F1301251880) ATO documentation  .
The application is provided as a Commercial-off-the-Shelf (COTS) application that runs in a single enclave with multiple agency tenants.  All customer data is stored in the same database instance.  Shared tenancy is built into the database with customer data so that each customer’s data is separated logically and protected from unauthorized access.  Shared tenancy is built into the database architecture of the software.  Economic Systems (EconSys) operates one instance for all customers in a virtual environment hosted in the Amazon Web Services (AWS) GovCloud, which is a High Categorization Gov Community Cloud.  One code set implements all application functionality, including customized features for agencies.

description: Instrument Flight Procedures (IFP) Routes is the tool for documenting route and airway segment data associated with instrument flight procedure development. This tool is intended to replace the current manual process in which Route information is documented and distributed.  This tool, as part of the Instrument Flight Procedure Automation (IFPA) suite of applications, will ensure that IFP Route information is documented in accordance with current published criteria, properly versioned, maintained in alignment with supporting aeronautical data for the estimated chart cycle, and guarantee only authorized personnel can modify the data at the appropriate steps in the IFP lifecycle.  The IFP Routes tool will also enable the IFP route data to be discoverable and exchanged in an industry recognized format, achieving the organizational goal of providing aeronautical information as a service.

name: Office of Information and Technology Hosting Services
fullname_0: Office of Information and Technology Hosting Services
description:
AIT Hosting Services General Support System (GSS) is the consolidated FISMA-reportable authorization boundary that incorporates the provisioning, deployment and maintenance support for servers and the underlying infrastructure and support tools such as the ESXi Hosts, Nutanix and vSphere hypervisor, Avamar backup, storage solutions and Enterprise Storage Area Network (SAN) devices in both the AIT EDC, Regional Offices and FAA Cloud Service (FCS) AWS and Azure hosting environments.  The boundary includes the power, environmental controls, rack space and physical security at the AIT EDC locations.  It also includes Trellix Suite (formerly McAfee) e-Policy Orchestrator (ePO).

Although the system is being renamed to AIT Hosting Services, the AIT data centers will still be referred to
as the AIT EDC (MMAC) & AIT EDC (WJHTC). In FY24, The AIT Hosting Services authorization boundary has been expanded to include AIF-420 support for certain FAA Cloud Services (FCS) support functions.  This includes provisioning of the FCS AWS Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) and the deployment of operating
systems in both FCS AWS and Microsoft Azure cloud environments.   AIT EDC does not include middleware applications (databases, e.g., Oracle, SQL), network components (e.g., routers, switches), or workstations and peripheral components (e.g., printers).  The management and responsibility of those items is included in separate authorization boundaries. 

Servers hosted within AIT Hosting Services are classified as either AIT Managed or Self-Managed based on the AIT Hosting Agreement put in place between the customer and AIF-400. Customer Self-Managed servers hosted within AIT Hosting Services locations are assessed within their own authorization boundaries.  Systems may inherit certain physical security controls from the data centers, AWS, Azure, and applicable cloud service providers.

AIF-420 provides infrastructure and operating system platforms for the various Business and Application owners throughout the FAA and provides them a stable operating environment in which to deploy their
applications.  AIF-420 directs and manages the provisioning of hosting solutions to FAA clients in a 24/7 environment.  AIF-420 provides remotely managed infrastructure services and hosted services including:

Server Management – Manages and administers virtual environments and performs administration activities on servers within the enterprise. AIF-420 and ADE-420 evaluate, manage, and administer virtual environments; perform administration activities on servers within the enterprise; manage server lifecycle; and plan for additional capacity.

 System Administration – Performs operating system installation, configuration, optimization, and support.  Performs system administration, maintenance, and patching at the operating system level and below.

Storage and Backup – Manages and maintains storage, backup, and archival solutions. Monitors systems to ensure recoverability and provides ad-hoc recovery services. AIF-420 and ADE-420 provide information on performance and planning for additional capacity. 

Hardware and Operating System Inventory Management – Manages inventory using BELARC, Tanium, and other inventory management tools.  

F5 – AIT EDC (MMAC basement, B03) hardware management only. The F5s hosted at the AIT EDC (MMAC 2ND floor) and AIT EDC (WJHTC) manage the configuration and SSL Certificates. 

Disaster Recovery Services – Manages and maintains servers to be used in a contingency situation.  Assists with the overall recovery effort in the event of a disaster.

name: FAA DroneZone - Drone Owners and Pilots - Registration
fullname_0: FAA DroneZone - Drone Owners and Pilots - Registration
description: The Unmanned Aircraft Systems Registration Service (UASRS) is used by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to provide small Unmanned Aircraft System (sUAS) operators/owners a service to register all sUAS for the purpose of operating sUAS in U.S. air space. sUAS are defined as those aircraft that weigh more than 0.55 pounds but less than 55 pounds. This service educates new operators about airspace rules so they can use their unmanned aircraft safely. As part of the registration process, registrants acknowledge that they have read, understand, and intend to follow the safety guidance. The service allows the FAA to identify and take enforcement action against those who intentionally violate the rules or operate unsafely.

name: Office of Information and Technology Networks
fullname_0: Office of Information and Technology Networks
description:
The AIT Networks system is a collection of AIT-managed Local Area Networks (LANs) that provide data transport among various lines of business within the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). The AIT Networks system exists for the purpose of data delivery, and provides connectivity to thousands of devices including servers, workstations, printers, applications, and other equipment.
AIT Networks boundary is defined to include devices that allow for network traffic transport, access control enforcement, Domain Name Service (DNS), wireless network infrastructure, and a number of maintenance systems. Most of the AIT Networks assets exist in the continental United States, with an exception for FAA LANs within the U.S. State Department embassies in Brussels, Belgium, and in the Republic of Singapore.  
AIT Networks system includes the following facility and geographical subdivisions:
•	FAA Regional Offices:
o	AAL Region- Alaska
o	ACE Region- Central
o	AEA Region- Eastern
o	AGL Region- Great Lakes
o	ANE Region- New England
o	ANM Region- Northwest Mountain
o	ASO Region- Southern
o	ASW Region- Southwest
o	AWA/HQ Region- Including Hangar 6
o	AWP Region- Western Pacific
•	ATO NAS Facilities:
o	Air Traffic Control Towers (ATCTs)
o	Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCCs)
o	Air Traffic Control Systems Command Center (ATCSCC)
•	Office of Aviation Safety (AVS) Sites:
o	Flight Standards District Offices (FSDO)
o	Manufacturer Inspection District Offices (MIDO)
o	Certificate Management Offices (CMO)
o	Field Locations
o	Aircraft Certification Offices (ACO)
o	Other offices
•	International Offices
•	William J. Hughes Technical Center (WJHTC)
•	AFN Infrastructure at Equinix DC-3/FCS Colo (formerly Terremark Data Center)
•	CSRA FCS Operations Control Center Bossier City, LA and Falls Church, VA 
AIT Networks includes the following sub-systems based on device type and functionality:
•	Cisco Access Control Server (Cisco ACS) – Used to centrally manage configuration of routers and switches within the boundary of Networks. 
•	Infoblox Domain Name Service (DNS) – A series of appliance that provide Domain Name Service (DNS) resolution to the Mission Support users. 
•	Active Directory DNS – Domain Name Service that runs on the Active Directory controllers.  
•	DNS Blacklist System - Records access attempts to a list of blacklisted websites, and presents a banner to the user instructing that an access policy violation has taken place. 
•	ForeScout Network Access Control (ForeScout NAC) – Restricts access to the Mission network to only authorized devices, and enforces compliance with a minimal AIS security baseline.
•	Routers and switches – Provides OSI Layer 2 and 3 routing and switching fabric for the Local LAN environments on Mission Support. 
•	Wireless Network – Provides IEEE 802.11 compliant wireless network access. The wireless network infrastructure consists of the following:
o	The Wireless Security & Spectrum Intelligence Module; 
o	Cisco 5508 Series Wireless Controller; and
o	Wireless Access Points.

5/14/2024 - Per Jill Longenecker:  ANDS is not part of the CPCS boundary or the IFPA boundary.  It also is not part of the AIT database boundary. As Teresa (Wilson) mentions, AIT databases is a GSS which means that it offers services to other systems.  Basically their database platforms host the databases but their boundary DOES NOT cover the data within the database.   AIT Databases will not take responsibility for ANDS data and ANDS is NOT covered by the AIT database boundary. Normally the data within a database is covered under the primary application that supports that database.  That’s what the meetings about ANDS have been about.  How to define that new boundary since ANDS and the majority of the applications using ANDS do NOT have a boundary and have never been assessed.  Please don’t take your eye off of the goal.  All security and privacy documentation ALWAYS center around the boundary and authority to operate (ATO).   Therefore, please press forward with defining the new boundary.  The most straight forward approach would to be to say x application owns the ANDS data and we are going to build a boundary and ATO around that.   But as we discussed in those meetings, there are other approaches on how to define this new boundary.  It is my understanding that Alvin JnBaptiste is taking the lead on this.  ATO security must be engaged to move this forward.

4/23/24 - Per John Hanson:  AJV-A is engaging with ATO Security and the AIT/ADE group to work on establishing an Authority To Operate for the Aeronautical Navigation Database System (ANDS).  In our research, we have not been able to determine where ANDS is listed as an independent investment, or how it is funded at all.  Seeing that it is operated from a database perspective by your group, do you know how the funding is channeled to your group for ANDS?  Is it F&E, Ops, or CIP maybe?  In anything you have seen, is ANDS ever mentioned as an independent investment?

notes:
8/10/21 Per FS Application Roadmap: • DCS is not an “application” in the traditional sense of the word; it is a service used to procure digital certificates – the procurement and annual renewal of certificates is done via the DCS Website. DCS is thought of as the “application” component.  The only actual users of DCS as an application are a few DCS Administrators.  All ~5,000 FAA inspectors and aviation industry representatives procuring digital certificates annually through DCS do not log in to DCS.
• All DCS work is paid for with WebOPSS funds. AFS-260 purchases and distributes digital certificates for all authorized personnel signing documents in WebOPSS and eForm 337 (and now OAPS) via DCS. Related costs also include annual fees for identity verification services for non-FAA personnel, and the purchase of annual digital certificates (annual licenses for ISO x.509-compliant PKI personal certificates) for distribution through DCS, currently about 5,000 per year. Another critical aspect of DCS maintenance is dedicated Tier 3 support to assist with digital certificate processing and troubleshooting service issues. Given DCS funding needs and the fact that it supports applications other than WebOPSS, DCS should be funded independent of WebOPSS.
• Additional costs include those for bug fixes and required functionality refinements needed. This includes security fixes identified in long-standing medium and high criticality POA&Ms. The list of POA&Ms is expected to increase after a full security scan is conducted on DCS.
• Tickets in JIRA are implemented via scheduled maintenance releases; however, a lot of needed work cannot be completed due to constant shortage of dedicated and qualified resources. Many of the tickets are related to security POA&Ms.
• FAA inspectors and industry users signing documents in WebOPSS and eForm eForm 337 and Safety Standards managers signing memos in OAPS procure digital certificates from DCS. It is hoped that DCS will be replaced with an enterprise-wide solution to procure and manage digital certificates where needed for digital signatures and documents/message authentication as needed across various applications.
• The ideal solution would be an agency-wide (or at a minimum, an AVS-wide) certificate authority solution to provide secure, trusted, identity-verified digital certificates to aviation industry partners to sign official FAA documents and forms.
• The standard for FAA users to authenticate documents should be the digital certificate stored on PIV cards. However, using PIV certificates must be balanced with cost considerations. It is currently cost prohibitive to change WebOPSS/OAPS/eForm 337 to use PIV-based authentication as opposed to digital certificates purchased via DCS.

name: Electronic Document Retrieval System II
description: EDRS II is AFS-750’s original electronic document retrieval system implemented prior to RMS. The application contains a subset of the aircraft images/documents stored in RMS/IMS and contains a set of older historical documents never introduced into RMS. Documents include aircraft airworthiness, registration, and suspense documents. This repository primarily fulfills document requests for entities outside of the Registry and separates that population from the RMS system to prevent access to special PII stored within RMS. Users have read-only access. RMS transmits daily image updates.Note: There is an on-site public user group called the "Public Documents Room". There are special hardware and software configurations applied to their GFE machines. They have a restricted, locked-down workstation configuration and they log into a Terminal Server infrastructure.

name: Alaska Boundary Connection
description:
The Alaska Boundary Connection (ABC) provides secure, network connectivity from the FAA internal administrative/mission support infrastructure to the Internet through Department of Interior (DOI) for the Alaskan Regional Office and other facilities within Alaska to perform administrative functions.

The Alaska Boundary Connection (ABC) system provides a single, permanent, logical connection to the Internet through a physical connection provided by the Department of the Interior (DOI). ABC relies on the DOI connection through General Communication, Inc. (GCI), as the Internet Service Provider (ISP) for Internet connectivity. As a Trusted Internet Connection, and similar to other FAA TICs, ABC is a set of switches, routers, firewalls, proxies, and supporting systems that provides secure access to the public Internet and hosts Demilitarized Zones (DMZs) for the Administrative Network Security Domain. The Weather Camera/ WARP system is a primary user of the ABC TIC.

name: Voluntary Safety Data Acquisition
description: Voluntary Safety Data Acquisition (VSDA) is the IT solution that supports both The Advanced Qualification Program (AQP), and ASAP. AQP is a voluntary alternative to the traditional regulatory requirements under CFR 14, Parts 121 and 135 for pilot training and checking. Under the AQP the FAA is authorized to approve significant departures from traditional requirements, subject to justification of an equivalent or better level of safety. The program entails a systematic front-end analysis of training requirements from which explicit proficiency objectives for all facets of pilot training are derivedIt seeks to integrate the training and evaluation of cognitive skills at each stage of a curriculum. For pass/fail purposes, pilots must demonstrate proficiency in scenarios that test both technical and crew resource management skills together. Air carriers participating in the AQP must design and implement data collection strategies which are diagnostic of cognitive and technical skills. In addition, they must implement procedures for refining curricula content based on quality control data.

name: ASKME Airworthiness Directives Development
description: ADD optimizes the development process for Airworthiness Directives (ADs) by providing work-flow, data storage and sharing capabilities. The Airworthiness Directive (AD) Development (Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (NPRM), Final Rules, Emergency Rules, Exemptions, Alternative Means of Compliance, and Synopsis) sub-function is one of two sub-functions under Function 2 - Airworthiness Directives. Ads are regulations developed and issued by the FAA to correct or prevent unsafe conditions. Each AD contains the following information: Description of the unsafe condition, Product to which the AD applies, Required corrective action and/or operating limitations, Compliance time, Where to obtain additional information, and Information on alternative methods of compliance with the requirements of the AD. FAA Order 8040.1 (Airworthiness Directives) specifies in detail the necessary procedures for issuing and complying with ADs.

name: ASKME Compliance and Enforcement Actions
description: Compliance and Enforcement Actions application provides process assistance / improvements for conducting investigation and enforcement activities. The Compliance and Enforcement Actions application is one of four sub-functions under Function 9 - Investigation and Enforcement. The FAA conducts an investigation to determine if enforcement actions need to be taken upon receipt of information indicating a possible rule or policy violation. The objective of the investigation is to collect enough information to determine whether or not an actual rule violation has occurred, and if so, what enforcement action needs to be taken to correct the violation. The supporting information collected may be in the form of interviews, photographs, charts, maps, diagrams, reports, records, physical evidence, and/or any other material that is legally obtainable. All of the evidence and findings are documented in the Enforcement Investigation Report. If it is determined that a violation has occurred, the Enforcement Investigation Report will state a recommended enforcement action. FAA Order 2150.3 (Compliance and Enforcement Program) specifies in detail the necessary procedures for conducting compliance and enforcement activities. CEA will automate the existing enforcement process and ensure process standardization and efficiency.

The DOT Interface Repository was designed and developed following the migration of DOT payroll and personnel processing to the Department of the Interior Federal Personnel and Payroll System (FPPS).  The Interface Repository (IR) is a subsystem of CASTLE that uploads and stores employee personnel and payroll data from the Department of Interior (DOI) and training data from the e-Learning Management System (eLMS ). The IR system serves as the centralized repository to provide a common data source for all interface data for DOT systems.

The DOT Interface Repository (DOT-IR) for federal employees is used to verify employee name and SSN information. The DOT Interface Repository (DOT IR) was created to load data from the host system and provide a source for applications that need data through a computer interface data from the DOT Interface Repository (DOT IR) and provides the various tertiary systems with the payroll data.

Per SCD dated April 2020:  The MMAC NET Security Authorization boundary includes the following: 
•	Cisco Networking Devices – Cisco routers and switches that provide the networking fabric for the Local LAN environments of the MMAC campus 
•	CheckPoint Firewalls – used for Access Control enforcement between various MMAC subnets 
•	F5 Load Balancers – used for load-balancing a variety of applications that are not included within the authorization boundary of the MMAC NET; however, the F5 devices themselves are managed by ESC 
•	Gigamon – allows for visibility into network traffic and dataflows via Test Access Points (TAPs) and Switch Port Analyzers/Mirrors (SPANs). Gigamon TAPs and SPANs allow for real-time complete or selective duplication of network packets used to create multiple data streams and used for Intrusion Detection monitoring in support of AIF, ADE and AIS organizations.
•	DNS – A FreeBSD Linux instance configured to provide DNS services for the MMAC campus 
•	Syslog Servers – Consists of Hebe and Hades systems. Hebe is used to store audit trails prior to their upload to the SOC ArcSight. The Hades server is used for archiving purpose, and retains audit trails for historical posterity. 
•	Cisco Prime – Used to manage and monitor the MMAC NET Cisco switching and routing devices. Integrated with Cisco Access Control Server (ACS), which is used to enforce centralized, Active Directory-based authentication via Terminal Access Controller Access Control System (TACACS+)
•	SolarWinds - Acts as a robust Enterprise monitoring platform that allows for continuous monitoring of systems and websites via a wide variety of mechanisms, including: dedicated probe or poller agents, SNMP, ping, event log collection/ analysis, and performance metric collection.
•	SolarWinds Database - SQL Server 2016 database used to store collected logs, metrics, and reports. 
•	Windows Systems – Consists of Windows 2008 R2 systems that are used to run the SolarWinds Primary and Secondary Pollers and the SolarWinds Database. Additionally, several Windows 2016 instances are used to host the CheckPoint Firewall Identity Collector 
•	Linux Systems – FreeBSD and Scientific Linux 6 instances used mainly for DNS, mail relay, and audit trail collection

name: ASKME Oversee System Performance
description: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Order 8000.369, Safety Management System, sets forth basic management principles to guide the FAA in safety management and oversight activities. The Order establishes an oversight function to monitor and effectively manage safety systems. The ASKME OSP application provides this oversight functionality to the Aircraft Certification Service (AIR). The ASKME OSP system is the vehicle by which AIR defines, collects, and analyzes safety data from the performance of certification activities. ASKME OSP facilitates proactive, data-driven, risk-based analysis and decision-making support to monitor the health of the AIR Safety Management System (SMS) and provides information to enable continuous SMS improvement. ASKME OSP does not have system connections to receive data. Instead, ASKME OSP users manually enter the information requested in a Data Call, e.g. the number of initial approved/accepted certification plans for Type Certificates (TCs) and Amended Type Certificates (ATCs) (those with a Form FAA 8110-12, Application for Type Certificate, Production Certificate, or Supplemental Type Certificate) issued in the reporting period. ASKME OSP users enter only the total count of these forms; they do not enter information from the form into the system.

name: Program Management System Tool
description:
PMST is a program, not a system, that contributes to the FAA's program management information processing capabilities related to modernization of the National Airspace System (NAS). The Program Management System Tools (PMST) is a software-only system that contributes to the FAA's program management information processing capabilities related to modernization of the National Airspace System (NAS).  Each of these systems facilitates a specific program management activity.  The PMST applications are:

Strategic Planning Implementation, Reporting, and Evaluation (SPIRE):

SPIRE is an FAA owned web-based application encompassing a set of integrated enterprise-class business capabilities used by the FAA to support and carry out key business needs. It is the single point of control and authoritative source for program management, strategic planning, budget formulation, execution, and financial management. SPIRE provides interactive, automated information and data, tracking, reporting, and management ability for the FAA along with supporting business plan formulation and performance tracking across the agency. SPIRE is the system of record for the following business capabilities:
Strategic Business Management (SBM)
Capital Investment Plan (CIP)
Budget Formulation Management (BFM)
Facilities and Equipment (F&E)
Research Engineering & Development (RE&D)
Program Information and Reporting (PIR)
ALA-300 Modeling, Analysis, and Reporting Tool ALAMART:
The ALAMART collects data from multiple sources, runs ALA-300 staffing models, increases analytical capabilities and data accessibility, and leverages the functionality available in software packages that the FAA owns. Its primary functions include gathering data in one central repository, cleansing and validating data, automating current manual or semi-automated processes, storing historical data to support trend analysis, and providing web-based reporting and analytical capabilities.
The data stored within the ALAMART feeds the models, applications, and reports built within the system.
FEDTool Connector:
The FEDTool Connector is owned by ABP-300 and pulls data from the SPIRE Portal database via a SPIRE Portal API on a nightly basis. The Connector operates as a wrapper around the web service API and serves as a reporting mart that provides data to the FEDTool dashboard.  The FEDTool Connector will provide a better capability for programs to access Cost, Schedule, and Business Planning information.
NOTE: FedTool is owned by APO-400.

name: ASKME Airworthiness Certification
description: An airworthiness certificate is an FAA authorization to operate an aircraft. Airworthiness certificates are classified as two basic types: standard airworthiness certificates and special airworthiness certificates. Special airworthiness certificates are: restricted, limited, and provisional airworthiness certificates; special flight permits; and experimental certificates. The following steps are followed to obtain a special airworthiness certificate: the applicant submits a formal application, FAA determines the aircraft meets eligibility requirements for the certificate requested, and FAA determines the aircraft is in a condition for safe operation. Then the FAA issues a special airworthiness certificate.FAA Order 8130.2 (Airworthiness Certification of Aircraft and Related Products) specifies in detail the necessary procedures for issuing an airworthiness certificate.

name: ATO Non-Federal Facilities Web Application
description:
The Advanced Systems Design Service (ASDS) Team, AJW-121, within Operations Support, Technical Operations, Air Traffic Operations, is responsible for implementing and managing the FAA’s Non-federal Program in accordance with 14 CFR Part 171, AC 150/5220-16, and 6700.20 Approval, Operation, and Oversight of Non-federal Systems. The ASDS team and the Non-federal Program ensure that Non-federal Airport Sponsors are maintaining their facilities to the appropriate standards.

The Non-federal (NONFED) Facilities Web Application was designed to provide a single repository for information and documentation associated with the oversight of non-federal systems. This allows FAA inspectors to maintain facility information, such as equipment type, FCC license information, and points of contact. The application also allows for the creation of annual inspection reports, maintenance agreements between the FAA and the sponsor, and detailed project information regarding pre-commissioning, decommissioning, and facility modifications.

name: Advanced Rotorcraft Simulator
description: ARS updates the VGARS to a technically advanced rotorcraft research simulator and a glass cockpit configuration representative of contemporary rotorcraft. A true Technically Advanced Rotorcraft (TAR) simulator will allow research performed in the Aerospace Human Factors Research Division to be generalized to the type of rotorcraft that are expected to be operating in the NextGen environment and which are currently being manufactured. This type of simulator will have, as its baseline configuration, large-format displays with an electronic primary flight display (with Synthetic Vision), Multi-Function Display (MFD) with at least terrain, weather, and traffic information. Critical upgrades include: 1) the ability to allow a second simulator operator to participate in the simulation as an air traffic controller, 2) a pseudo pilot function that enables the control of vehicles, both air and ground, that are external to the simulated helicopter and are operating in the same simulated spaced, 3) use electric control loaders (not hydraulic) to represent realistic pressure feedback to all flight controls in all flight configurations , and 4) would allow the loading and use of other aero models by the users (ideally this would use an interactive database that included a defined set of variables felt to be sufficient to generally define an aircraft's performance for FAA test purposes, with an editing capability that would allow alternate aero models to be loaded into the system and used in place of the basic supplied aero model). Upgrading to a true TAR simulator will allow the scientists to conduct research using a platform that both represents rotorcraft existing in and continuing to enter the rotorcraft fleet, and it will provide a familiar platform for participants on which even more technical advances can be evaluated. ARS will support real-time collection of a large range of performance-related variables and allow introduction/simulation of cutting-edge rotorcraft systems. The current simulator was developed in house in 1998. ARS will replace the legacy VGARS with a next-generation rotorcraft model using current computer technologies with a sustainable & modifiable architecture. It will support research on: Advanced displays (flight, navigation, weather, data uplink); Advanced controls; Digital air-to-ground communication (traffic, clearances, flight routes); and Procedures, pilot capabilities, and training requirements.

name: Air Traffic Control Advanced Research Simulator
fullname_0: Air Traffic Control Advanced Research Simulator
description: This is a high fidelity definition tower cab simulator and integrated eye-movement recorder for human-in-the-loop (HITL) system evaluation, information requirements collection, and training tool development.  It replaces the Tower Simulation-Based Performance Measure (TSBPM) and a Mobile Eye eye-movement recorder.  The TSBPM is a medium fidelity simulator that operates on one personal computer (PC) driving five 21 monitors.  It is capable of representing up to 180 degrees of out-the-window view, has no play-back capabilities, and does not come with an instruction manual or customer support as is was developed at the FAA Academy.  The Mobile Eye eye-movement recorder is a portable head mounted eye-tracker that, for tracking scan patterns, requires manual data coding.  The TSBPM will be replaced by a high fidelity tower cab simulator and the Mobile Eye will be replaced by a workstation mounted eye-movement recorder.  The replacement tower cab simulator will use ten 52 monitors to provide a 360 degree out-the -window view, record files for playback, and include an option for training and customer support.  The replacement eye-movement recorder will enable the creation of a digital model of the environment enabling automated data coding and, since it is not head mounted, allow controller participants to control simulated traffic without being hindered by the glare inherent with having extra lenses between the controller's eyes and the monitors.  Expanded research requirements have led to a need for increased functionality in the original TSBPM.  It was determined that the tower simulation functionality needed to be increased to allow the TSBPM to provide improved training capabilities rather than just collecting responses to multiple choice questions. In addition, it is necessary to run human-in-the-loop simulations in a tower environment to support research on human factors issues in NextGen tower cabs.  For example, studies will be performed concerning tower controller scan patterns and out the window information requirements.  Also will be used with other measures to gauge controller workload and situation awareness in conditions of increased automation; validation of the  FAA’s controller selection tool (the AT-SAT); high fidelity scanning behavior studies; ATC time on task performance; evaluation of NextGen tools; and prototype tools to train recovery after error.

name: General Air Traffic and Technical Operations Research Laboratory
fullname_0: General Air Traffic and Technical Operations Research Laboratory
description: The Reconfigurable Medium-Fidelity Air Traffic Controller (ATC) and Technical Operations Selection Research Laboratory was originally configured to support ATC selection research. Selection research is no longer a focus for AAM-520. In order to support new research requirements examining ATC performance and the effects of automation in Technical Operations, replacements for the workstations (> 50) and updates to the software and network are needed to ensure the protection of personally identifiable information (PII). Currently, the server for the data collection laboratory and the data server are isolated from the FAA network; however, these data are vulnerable when they are in transit. While adequate protection is in place, the importance of adopting a proactive strategy becomes more important as FAA systems are brought under one domain. The use of one domain provides the agency with cost saving and transparency, but the danger of an unintentional or, worse yet, an intentional breach of our data systems increases with the number of workstations with access to our systems through the network. It is proposed therefore that both servers be replaced to provide static and on-the-fly encryption of data and that the data server be connected to the researchers work areas via a private network. For the laboratory, a secure server for the virtual private network is necessary. The data collected in the laboratory do not reside on the laboratory server for longer than 24 hours, so an actual private network is not required. Additionally, several software updates are needed. The current selection battery for Air Traffic Control Specialists (ATCSs), the Air Traffic Selection and Training (AT-SAT) test battery will not run on an operating system later than Windows 7. Also, updates for research software to include voice recognition and 3-D capabilities are needed to allow research to support NextGen. . These technical refreshes would allow studies of teamwork in ATC environment and the development of technical operations simulations relative to Operations Control Centers (OCC). GATTOR will be used for the Measurement and Improvement of Performance in Air Traffic and Technical Operations Specialists. For example, to develop performance measures for both individual specialists and the systems with which they work; identify both cognitive and non-cognitive factors that predict performance of ATC and Technical Operations (Tech Ops) specialists; assess the effects of alternative programs, procedures, and other experimental treatments on ATC/Tech Ops specialist performance; and development of longitudinal databases using very large research data files. Source: AMEN Equipment list for FID (DP S302), dated January 2015.

name: Technically Advanced General Aviation Research Simulator
fullname_0: Technically Advanced General Aviation Research Simulator
description: TAGARS updates the AGARS to a technically advanced general aviation research simulator and a glass cockpit configuration representative of contemporary General Aviation (GA) aircraft.  A true Technically Advanced Aircraft (TAA) simulator will allow research performed in the Aerospace Human Factors Research Division to be generalized to the type of aircraft that are expected to be operating in the NextGen environment and which are currently being manufactured.  This type of simulator will have, as its baseline configuration, large-format displays with an electronic primary flight display (with Synthetic Vision), Multi-Function Display (MFD) with at least terrain, weather, and traffic information, and an integrated autopilot that can be driven by the navigation engine of the MFD/map.  The additional benefit will be that as more pilots either transition to or receive ab initio training in TAA cockpits, fewer will be familiar with legacy cockpits and instrumentation.  Thus, more and more participants in future research will expect the TAA cockpit as the standard.  Upgrading to a true TAA simulator will allow the scientists to conduct research using a platform that both represents aircraft existing in and continuing to enter the GA fleet, and it will provide a familiar platform for participants on which even more technical advances can be evaluated.  TAGARS will support real-time collection of a large range of performance-related variables and allow introduction/simulation of cutting-edge aircraft systems.  The current simulator is the oldest in the research laboratory (both computer technology and aircraft simulated; Piper Malibu).  TAGARS will replace the legacy AGARS with a next-generation aircraft model using current computer technologies with a sustainable & modifiable architecture.  It will support research on: Advanced displays (flight, navigation, weather, data uplink); Advanced controls (manual, automated, envelope protection); Digital air-to-ground communication (traffic, clearances, flight routes); and Procedures, pilot capabilities, and training requirements.  The additional $325.5K (incl. $500, $5000, $20000) concerns communications upgrades: Since inception the air traffic control workstations and flight deck simulators have simulated communications due to technological limitations. The technology is now available to upgrade the respective simulators so that the air traffic control workstations and the flight deck simulators can communicate in real time. This increases the face validity of the research program and has been requested by multiple sponsors of research.   The additional $360.5 K (incl. $500, $10,000, $20,000, 30,000) concerns a dome: The 220 Degree Moving Display, replaces 8 monitors that have been used for out-the-window displays. The 220 degree moving display provides a seamless out-the-window visual that provides appropriate vestibular stimulation to simulate the movement of the aircraft and environmental conditions. The 220 degree moving display is a wrap around dome screen with a support structure for projectors. It can be moved to different simulator locations and adjusted to multiple simulators. The updated displays will support research on: Advanced displays (flight, navigation, weather, traffic); Advanced controls (manual, automated, envelope protection); Digital air-to-ground communication (traffic, clearances, flight routes); and Procedures, pilot capabilities, and training requirements.

name: Asset Marking System Field Spares Inventory
fullname_0: Asset Marking System Field Spares Inventory
description:
FAA has re-instituted the Field Spares Inventory (FSI) Program to provide an accurate and complete inventory of field spares through a continuous inventory process to support the FAA's goals for integrated and optimized supply chains. The FSI Program is establishing an initial (baseline) initiative and follow-on maintenance of field spares which will move the FAA toward the enterprise-wide availability to view and make decisions based on available spares inventories at both the depot (using LCSS) and field levels (using AMS). 
The field spares inventory process in AMS has two phases. The first phase is to establish location records in AMS and then print and attach location 2D barcodes to those physical locations. The location hierarchy is building, room, cabinet, shelf, and bin. In the second phase, the spare asset record is established in AMS where AMS leverages pre-existing asset and facility data from LCSS and FSEP, respectively. Therefore, loading an asset includes selecting key data (e.g., NSN and GSA address) that can look up the applicable records from these sources. Creating a spare asset record requires scanning the location barcode to associate the spare asset to its current location.

name: eVerify
description: An OMB-mandated system that verifies, through information on the I-9, an individual’s right to work. E-Verify provides federal and non-federal employers with “Instant Verification of Employment Eligibility”. It is an Internet-based system that compares information from an employee's Form I-9, Employment Eligibility Verification, to data from U.S. Department of Homeland Security and Social Security Administration records to confirm employment eligibility. E-Verify is the only free, fast, online service of its kind that verifies employees' data against millions of government records and provides results within as little as three to five seconds.

name: Reasonable Accommodation Management System
description: The purpose of this system is to track reasonable accommodation requests submitted by DOT employees and applicants. DOT is required to collect information on accommodation requests and report annually whether requested accommodations were provided or denied within the allowable time frame (a maximum of 25 business days). The system will assist all decision makers in ensuring that a decision is made and the accommodation is provided within the time frame allowed. Access to the system is controlled by user credentials maintained in a secure database. All personally identifiable information maintained in the system is encrypted. RAMS replaces the previous OnLine Accommodation Tracking System (OATS).

name: Workforce Tracking System
description: WTTS allows supervisors or HR specialists to create and track vacancies in advance of creation of SF52 actions. Personnel and payroll information is sent real time to FPPS, eliminating the need for HR to re-enter data into FPPS. This results in generation of SF52 actions in FPPS directly from WTTS. It is also one-stop shopping for real-time status of vacancies, announcements, and on-boarding with data from automated staffing systems, FPPS, and EODS. Authorized users (supervisors, HR specialists, security, and facilities) can view the entry on duty date and location for new hires. WTTS has real time interfaces with FPPS and two automated staffing systems—Monster's Enterprise Hiring Management and OPM's USA Staffing.

name: Air Traffic Operations Management System
description: ATOMS (Air Traffic Operations Management System) is a solution which tracks, in real-time, the work assignments of Air Traffic Controllers. It tracks air traffic controller’s shifts, work activities, airspace responsibility, leave, training, and breaks. As a key component of Air Traffic Operations, it provides managers and supervisors with real-time dashboards showing staff assignments and mapping work activities to payroll and financial budgeting. The solution provides configuration of complex business rules, both nationally and locally, and allows users to customize the user interface to meet the needs of their facility (or location). ATOMS integrates will key systems used for reporting, payroll, and LDR (Labor & Distribution Reporting).

Agencies also may provide eOPF access to special investigators, helping to speed the investigation process and save agency resources.

name: Human Resources Management Suite
description: HRMS is a suite of modules, also called bolt-ons (HRMS Modules), a System Integration Framework (HRMS SIF), and a set of standardized integration connectors.   Currently the modules that are operational are: Electronic Contractor Staffing System (eCstaffing), Entrance on Duty System (EODS), Talent Management System (TMS), and Workforce Transformation and Tracking System (WTTS).  IBC also offers discounted purchase of Automated Staffing Licenses through Monster's Enterprise Hiring Management, and OPM's USA Staffing.  An eRecruitment connector is operational, providing real time integration between 3rd-party automated staffing systems, EODS, WTTS, and the Federal Personnel Payroll System (FPPS).  The vision of the IBC's Human Resources Management Suite (HRMS) is to significantly improve the federal governments' business processes for management of human resources (HR) through seamless, end-to-end, real-time integration between HR and other systems, using Simple Object Access Protocol based web services. This provides single point data capture eliminating redundant data entry, and real-time sharing of data with other systems needing the data, resulting in efficiency gains, improved quality of data, and increased employee satisfaction. Standards based integration sockets support the concept of plug-and-play, allowing HRMS to integrate with solutions from a variety of vendors and federal HR Shared Service Centers (SSCs).

name: Tower Simulation System
description: The Tower Simulation System (TSS) is a virtual training system for control tower facility training programs located at Air Traffic Control (ATC) facilities. The TSS provides initial in-the-field, proficiency and recertification training for working controllers in addition to training with live air traffic in accordance with Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Order 3120.4  Air Traffic Technical Training. The TSS supports up to four simultaneous trainee positions including local, ground, flight data/clearance delivery, and coordinator. The simulator provides synthetic voice response and voice recognition to allow the student to interact with the simulator. The voice recognition system interprets the student's commands and translates them into actual aircraft movement depicted visually on the screen. A recorded playback feature allows instructors to review and evaluate performance and provide feedback to the student after the training session. The TSS is also used in non-training applications. 59 TSSs currently deployed at 42 sites (and added 42 mobile TSS) supporting 256 tower facilities.  It is a stand-alone application that does not connect to the Internet.

name: BasedAircraft
description:
Airports Program Suite (APS) consists of two applications: CCMISNet and BasedAircraft. 

BasedAircraft.com is a web-based inventory application with approximately 200,000 based aircraft operating at over 2,900 National Plan of Integrated Airports System (NPIAS) airports nationwide. Tadera/GCR is responsible for the overall management of the nationwide data collection process, development of the system, maintaining the data, and establishing the web-enabled application to allow the FAA to view the aircraft inventory at each NPIAS airport.
The information contained in ba.com is designated "Security Sensitive Information" because the aggregate data provides a potential security risk and is not available to the public. Tadera's application provides a real-time analysis of N numbers received from the airports identifying which aircraft are not in the FAA's aircraft registration database, those with expired registration, and those aircraft claimed to be based at multiple airports. After verifying and validating this data, the final aircraft data is searchable by the FAA staff (and limited to users authorized by FAA) through the web-enabled application.

name: FAA Financial Disclosure System
description: FDOnline is an electronic filing (e-filing) application that enables FAA personnel to enter financial disclosure information into a consolidated database. FDOnline supports the agency’s mission by providing a single collection point for the financial disclosure information of all employees obligated to meet this requirement.  Information is collected on OGE forms (specifically the OGE 278, OGE 450, and OGE 450a forms) for review by designated FAA ethics officials. They determine compliance with applicable Federal conflict-of-interest laws and regulations and identify if potential conflicts of interest exist between individuals employed by the Federal government and their outside employment and financial interests. FDOnline is a COTS application that is approved by the U.S. Office of Government Ethics.  FDOnline is licensed by the Office of Chief Counsel (AGC) from the vendor, HRWorx, for use within the FAA.

name: QUASAR
description: QUASAR is a  workflow web application used to automate business processes that support the AVS Quality Management System (QMS) and several Flight Standards oversight processes.  QUASAR application is developed under QMITS rewrite project which is a project replacement of the legacy QMITS application ( COTS product)  being run on Lotus Domino Platform ( which is going to be phased out of FAA). This application directly supports the AVS ISO 9001:2008 certification. Action Requests (AR), Corrective Action Requests (CAR), Preventive Action Requests (PAR), and Nonconformance Records (NCRs), Consistency and Standardization Initiative (CSI), and Stakeholder Feedback (SF) are recorded and tracked in QUASAR. Additionally, there is one AFS-specific workflow, Flight Standards Evaluation Program (FSEP), automated in QUASAR. CSI records are not a part of QUASAR.

name: FAA Cloud Services Colocation Services
description:
The FAA Cloud Services (FCS) Colocation Service contract includes the implementation, operation, and maintenance of data center facilities for colocation services. Colocation services refer to capabilities provided by General Dynamics Information Technology (GDIT), to host FAA-owned and operated Administrative/Mission Support Operational Domain systems at Equinix data center facilities. The FAA retains control and ownership of the Government Furnished Equipped (GFE) computing infrastructure, applications, and data residing within the colocation space. For the FCS Colocation space, GDIT, in coordination with the Equinix, provides full access to the FCS caged space within the Equinix facility for the FAA to install, provision and test the FAA’s GFE.
The FCS Colocation Services provide the data center physical and environmental protections including the caged area, rack space, FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure (FTI) Wide Area Network (WAN) connection, and power within an enclosed floor to ceiling cage at two Equinix data centers (Ashburn, Virginia and Sunnyvale, California) for FAA systems relocating to the FCS Colocation space. The FAA is responsible for the assessment and authorization of any systems/applications moving into the colocation space.

Per Don Birdwell:  We are having to migrate through the versions to support the additional components used by our applications. 
Upgrading to version 5.2.2 requires significant modifications in AccessAML to integrate with the Crowd REST API and update Spring-related libraries. We transitioned to version 4.4.6 as a temporary measure. This version requires fewer changes to existing applications, allowing continued functionality without extensive modifications. The plan is to use this interim period to thoroughly plan and implement the necessary changes for version 5.2.2. This includes ensuring compatibility with the Crowd REST API and updating Spring libraries. We have made these changes in our development environment and they are ready for testing.

name: Air Traffic Safety Action Program
description:
ATSAP is a non-punitive, voluntary safety reporting program designed to identify and report all events that may or did lead to a breakdown in safety or increase risk to air traffic operations. The program serves as one leg of a good Safety Management System.  ATSAP provides a systematic approach for Controllers and others providing or supporting the provision of air traffic services (per MOU with NATCA) including Air Traffic Assistants and Flight Data Communications specialists (per MOU with NAGE)as well as managers when engaged in providing air traffic control services. It also supports the analysis and Event Review Committee (ERC) functions and provides a messaging module to allow communications within the program and with individual submitters.

ATSAP Data Request form site is an ATSAP component that provides links to the Data Request process and forms. 
 ATSAP Data Requests can be used to provide information in response to Corrective Action Requests, and for Safety Risk Management panels, procedural workgroups or validation of existing safety strategies and risk mitigations. As the database expands and matures, ATSAP data parameters also allows for benchmarking operations and continuous analysis to discover vulnerabilities in the NAS.

ATSAP-X is an ATSAP component that provides Architects, Engineers, Service Center Staff Support Specialists, Aviation Technical Systems Specialists, and Flight Procedures Team personnel with a vehicle to voluntarily report events/ safety problems that may or did lead to a breakdown in safety or increase risk in the NAS. ATSAP-X also supports the analysis and event review committee (ERC) functions and provides a messaging module to allow communications within the program and with individual submitters. ATSAP-X began in May 2015.

Confidential Information Share Program (CISP) is an ATSAP component that provides a communication portal to allow air traffic controllers’ confidential reports to be shared with an airline’s voluntary reporting program, and pilots’ reports from the airlines’ programs to be shared with ATSAP. The purpose of the Confidential Information Share Program (CISP) is to demonstrate the benefit of conducting proactive safety assessments through the sharing and analysis of information collected through the Air Traffic Safety Action Program (ATSAP) and airlines' Aviation Safety Action Programs (collectively ASAP). These programs support the collection, assessment, and review of safety events from the perspectives of air traffic controllers and pilot.

name: Airports External Portal
description: External facing web site that provides the capability for authorized external users limited PFC and AIP project planning functions and data through an Internet connection using a desk top browser. This module allows public agencies (PAs) to enter their revenue and disbursement information into the automated system. It also provides limited Passenger Facility Charge (PFC) functionality and data, as described above, geared toward the needs of authorized external users. AEP also provides access to pre-generated reports meant for external users as well as five (5) reports that are publicly available (log in is not required to access these reports). These reports allow users to view pre-generated reports regarding the collection of PFC for certain periods, interest accrued and revenue. Reports generated that are publicly available are: Active vs. Inactive PFC Applications, Distribution of Projects Report, and Enplanements by Air Carrier for Calendar Year, Excluded Class of Carrier, and Revenue Summary Report. No PII data is included in any External SOAR reports.

name: SOAR Internal
description: SOAR Internal consists of a series of modules. The AIP module supports two (2) major functional requirements: Grants Management and Financial Accounting.  The Grants Management function tracks and reports on the progress of the grant: From the initiation of a grant; its review, up to and including, the Office of the Secretary of Transportation (OST); the award of the grant; and final close out.  The Financial Accounting function maintains fund accounts for a wide variety of purposes to ensure that funds are distributed as required by the legislation, and that they are properly accounted for, and reported in, an annual report.  The ACAIS module collects and processes data for air carriers and airports, supports the decision process concerning the determination of grant qualifications and entitlements, and calculates AIP passenger and cargo entitlements for eligible and qualifying airports resulting in approximately one-third of the overall AIP funding. The NPIAS module tracks the cargo and passenger landings for an airport in the NPIAS to determine the amount of entitlement funds.  This module consists of data entry and reporting to track the cargo and passenger landings for a given calendar year. The PFC module tracks airport improvement applications and their projects from a public agency's initial request to impose passenger facility charges on airline tickets through the use of those funds for eligible projects.  PFC is not a funds disbursement system, but a system used to monitor the PAs PFC program process, progress of projects, and to monitor PFC collections and interest earned. Work codes are assigned to PFC projects determining PFC eligibility, performance tracking, and reporting.

name: BMC ITSM Bundle
description:
This is the ITSM Bundle that acts as a single point of contact for user requests, user-submitted incidents, and infrastructure-generated incidents. It includes Incident Management and Problem Management. The focus of Incident Management is break/fix and concentrates on restoring the user’s IT capabilities. The focus of Problem Management is to determine the root cause of an incident then, using Change Management and its processes, correct the root cause. Incident and Problem cases can be related to other cases or to CIs or Change Requests.
The following features are in use and are part of this bundle: 
 BMC Asset Management, BMC Service Level Management, BMC Service Request Management BMC, Atrium Configuration Management Database and Smart Reporting .

name: AJI Safety Applications System
description:
This is a Parent System (authorization) for multiple applications that are contained within this Security Authorization.  The Office of Safety Evaluations (Safety Evaluations) is responsible for conducting audits, program assessments and evaluations of Air Traffic Control facilities to ensure the safety, quality, and efficiency of the air traffic control system. To accomplish this objective Safety Evaluations developed a new facility evaluation process which includes an independent audit process. The new process consists of annual internal facility evaluations (IFE) and periodic audits conducted by Safety Evaluations (ATO-S). 

In order to streamline the audit process the Facility Safety Assessment System (FSAS) was created.  FSAS is a web-based application and has facilitated implementation of the process by: 

•	Creating a tailored checklist of safety (as well as compliance) related items that will be assessed during IFEs and safety audits.
•	Giving facilities an opportunity to emphasize issues they want to bring to the attention of District, Service Area, or Headquarters management. 
•	Building a central repository of IE/audit data to monitor safety performance across the NAS and share successful risk mitigation strategies. 
•	Automating support for facility assessments conducted by ATC facilities, TMUs, and the Safety Evaluations group. Periodic safety audits and annual IFEs include safety-related topics spanning operational, quality assurance, training and administrative areas for ATC and TMU operations. 
•	Monitoring timelines for mitigation plan development, pending mitigation action(s) and progress toward certification of IFEs. 
•	Enhancing visibility into prominent NAS-wide mitigation issues. 
•	Maintaining integrity of the rating item catalog, including alignment of the rating item catalog in FSAS with the Configuration Control Board (CCB) catalog specifications.

The following are the current AJI Safety Apps/Tools:
•	ATO Manager Dashboards (MSD)
•	Business Objects Access Request (BOAR)
•	Alert Notices Repository (ALNOT)
•	Compliance Verification - Air Traffic (CVT-AT)
•	Line Up and Wait Worksheet (LUAW)
•	Common Post Events Checklist (CPEC)
•	Events Investigations Manager Console (EIMC)
•	Safety Investigations Database (SIDB)
•	In-Service Review Checklist Tool (ICT)
•	Independent Safety Assessment (ISA)
•	Barrier Analysis Review (BAR)
•	Shared Application for Factor Evaluation (SAFE)
•	Data Collection Tool (DCT)
•	Service Integrity Barrier Analysis Review (SIBAR)
•	Surface Risk Analysis Process (SRAP)
•	Runway Safety Tool (RST3)
•	Runway Safety Tracking System (RSTS)
•	Safety Management Tracking System (SMTS)

description:

FLEET-Builder forecasts the acquisition and deployment of aircraft on a global network. The tool leverages operations data to develop a base year of operations between airports for the passenger, business and freighter markets. The tool forecasts fleet growth and replacement, deployment and operation on the global network with associated energy and economic factors quantified. The tool also outputs data that can be imported into FAA's AEDT modeling system.

name: Administrative Personnel Action Tool
description:
APAT enables new efficiencies in the preparation and tracking of personnel action paperwork by offering:
Single form entry, full packet generation. APAT takes fields that duplicate across multiple personnel action forms and consolidates them into a single form for entry. Depending on the nature of actions, only the relevant fields appear.
Active directory sync and pre-population of key fields. Several features, such as name lookup in FAA’s current employee directory, pre-population of many required FPPS fields and cascading drop-down menus reduce the potential for manual-entry errors and expedite form completion. 
Searchable JAT and PD libraries. APAT’s flexible JAT and PD libraries store AHR-classified an commonly used JATs and PDs, as well as allow for quick modification and storing of new JATs and PDs.
Electronic signatures and routing. Rather than paper folders being carried from desk to desk, APAT routes the documents electronically for digital signature. APAT’s flexible workflow features enable customized levels of approval, depending on the organization’s needs.
Line item security. Managers and analysts see only those actions that they have in process or which they normally would facilitate.
Automated reporting. APAT provides the status of any given action at any point in the process. Additionally, actions in APAT automatically roll up to dashboards that offer analytics on position management, action volume, time-to-completion and other metrics that will facilitate continuous business process improvement.
