name: NASQuest
description:
NASQuest system that is run by the AJM-25 organization at the FAA Technical Center.  The NASQuest system is a web interface to a custom MySQL database system used to search Common Message Set (CMS) data for a variety of purposes including data reduction and analysis, generating simulation and playback scenarios, and preferred route analysis.  
The NASQuest system is an ATO NAS operational support system that provides NAS support services to a wide range of FAA users.  The NASQuest system primarily resides on the FAA Mission Support LAN with components in the FAA IAP DMZ to support external contractors/customers.  All of the NASQuest servers are running Scientific Linux v6.8 (Red Hat equivalent).  There are many data consumers of the data . .  

NASQuest is a non-NAS reporting system that uses NAS data.  It is similar to National Offload Program (NOP). NASQuest siphons common message set data off the NAS, organizes it into accessible data, and provides reports for second level engineering for AJM.  The system resides on the administrative or mission support LAN.

name: Digital Obstacle File
description:
This scheduled report system creates report files (based on the OAS DB info) that contain all known man-made obstructions that penetrate Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 77 within the U.S. and its territories. It also contains known obstacles within the Caribbean, Mexico, Canada and the Pacific. It is prepared and posted on this website every 56 days and it includes the latitude and longitude, structure type, height above ground, height above sea level, lighting, marking, accuracy code, and other associated information.
The Obstacles Team investigates and evaluates existing obstacles that may be hazardous to safe flight navigation. We receive obstacle data from a variety of sources both inside and outside the FAA. After determining proof of a completed structure by receiving supporting documentation and performing all necessary verification checks, the team assigns an accuracy code to the obstacle and enters it into the Obstacle Authoritative Source (OAS) as verified.

Aeronautical Information Services has provided greater public access to obstacle information by adding the obstacle information contained within the Digital Obstacle File (DOF) to the existing Aeronautical Data Delivery Service (ADDS). The ADDS site provides the functionality to filter by attributes and save in industry standard formats. Information is also available as a service.

It is prepared and posted on the website every 56 days and it includes the latitude and longitude, structure type, height above ground, height above sea level, lighting, marking, accuracy code, and other associated information.

OAS---feeds to--->DOF---feeds to --->ADDS
(ref: https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/flight_info/aeronav/obst_data/ )

name: Terraform
description:
Terraform is a tool for building, changing, and versioning infrastructure safely and efficiently. Terraform can manage existing and popular service providers as well as custom in-house solutions.

Configuration files describe to Terraform the components needed to run a single application or your entire datacenter. Terraform generates an execution plan describing what it will do to reach the desired state, and then executes it to build the described infrastructure. As the configuration changes, Terraform is able to determine what changed and create incremental execution plans which can be applied.

The infrastructure Terraform can manage includes low-level components such as compute instances, storage, and networking, as well as high-level components such as DNS entries, SaaS features, etc.

Operations Network (OPSNET) is the FAA’s official source for providing National Airspace System (NAS) “daily delay reporting as well as airport traffic counts and instrument operations”. The Performance Data, Analysis and Reporting System (PDARS) provides a means for field facility personnel and FAA offices to develop recommendations for improving the NAS through identification of capacity and system efficiency improvements to reduce delays. The combined program (still referred to as OPSNET-R merged with DVARS) has replaced the legacy OPSNET and PDARS systems with integrated flight visualization and performance analysis capabilities leveraging integrated flight trajectories, information, and metrics. The integrated system has leveraged enterprise resources, industry standards, and commercially available technology.

name: ATLAS Aviation
description:
FAA Airmen Knowledge Testing is part of the Airmen Certification process. AFS-630 has been developing the multiple choice Airmen Knowledge Tests in-house and outsourced test delivery with PSI Online for the last several years. With the FAA Airmen Testing Standards (ATS) applications past their useful life, AFS-630 awarded a full-service contract to PSI, with assistance from psychometricians, to develop, deliver, and manage the Airmen Knowledge Tests with new questions and scenarios. ATLAS will be used to deliver the tests. 
The FAA service contract with PSI was awarded for 10 years (3 base years and 7 option years) and is a zero-cost contract to the government as long as changes to ATLAS are not out of scope. PSI will make their money by collecting $150 fee per applicant test. AIT does not manage or support ATLAS, PSI does.
PSI will manage and store all testing data for ATLAS in-house with no current plans for Cloud deployment. To host ATLAS in the Cloud, PSI must be a FedRAMP-certified Cloud Service Provider. FedRAMP is the government’s most rigorous security compliance framework. 
Applicant test results will be sent from ATLAS to the Integrated Airman Certification and Rating Application (IACRA) via an outbound interface. This interface will use the Web service currently being developed for IACRA. 
A reporting structure between ATLAS and SPAS is also expected to be implemented in order to support Part 141 and 147 training centers ATS data usage in SPAS. However, what the interface will look like is currently unknown.

name: Oracle Business Intelligence Data Warehouse
description:
The Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) Office of Finance and Management (AFN) requires the capability to run and print reports from a centralized reporting tool to support their financial business functions and missions.  The Oracle Business Intelligence Data Warehouse (OBIDWH) system provides a central data warehouse and reporting capability for data received from other systems.  OBIDWH will receive data from the following systems:
•	Delphi: Department of Transportation (DOT) financial management system,
•	Logistics Center Support System (LCSS): FAA inventory and parts management system, and 
•	FAA Purchase Request Information System (PRISM): FAA's comprehensive procurement management system.
The OBIDWH data warehouse is based on a Commercial Off-the-Shelf (COTS) reporting tool titled the Oracle Exadata Database Machine (Exadata).  Exadata is a combined computing and storage system available for running Oracle Database software and provides reporting capabilities.  The FAA plans to create a standard set of reports within OBIDWH so that users can run the required reports from one centralized data warehouse. 
For its initial release, OBIDWH will be used as a reporting tool for data from the FAA System Logistics Center Support System (LCSS) and will go live in FY2019. The initial users of OBIDWH will be the Office of Finance and Management (AFN) users.  Subsequent users will be added, including all FAA users who formerly used the DOT Delphi system and the FAA PRISM system to run reports.  These users will be added to the list once OBIDWH receives its Authority to Operate (ATO).

name: Automated Periodic Review
description: APR receives scheduled jobs from the IFP Periodic Review (IFP PR) system for the periodic review of instrument flight procedures (IFPs) in accordance with FAA Order 8260.19.  APR then pulls necessary aeronautical data (e.g. airports, navaids, approach, obstacles) from the appropriate data source (e.g. IFPA-AIT) and runs an evaluation of the procedure using current criteria defined if FAA 8260 series.  The result of the evaluation (e.g. file to view the procedure design in TARGETS, evaluation results) are sent back to the IFP PR system to be stored with the record and for the IFP Specialist to adjudicate.

name: FAA Acquisition System Toolset Modernization
description: FAA Acquisition System Toolset (FAST) is the central location for all FAA information (including policy, guidance, templates, reference libraries) relating to Acquisition Management System (AMS) processes and procedures.  This system is a public facing source for all FAA Lifecycle Acquisition documents.  The FAA Acquisition System Toolset (FAST) is in need of a content management system to allow adding, editing, and deleting of website content through a user workflow.  This will also allow the content to be published by a system administrator to the website in batches, or as needed for maintenance.  This system would also provide a history document of summarized changes, redlined content changes, and a set of complete and readily available archives.  The current FAST update system/process relies on a 3rd party contractor to process manual change documents that limits flexibility and timeliness to prepare and publish revisions.  The proposed modernization effort would move the FAST to a managed service solution and allow for real-time review and publishing of AMS updates.

name: FAA Process Automation Environment
description:
FRAME is the parent System of the Citizen Development offerings in the CDFO (ADE-130).  FRAME provides the underlying infrastructure where the FAA may build, deploy, and monitor automations and applications.

FRAME is made up of commercial products running in the FAA Cloud Service (FCS) East/West Public Cloud Environment, specifically, UiPath and Blue Prism.  FRAME provides the underlying infrastructure where the FAA may build, deploy, and monitor automations.  Users of FRAME are required to use a well-defined process to plan for and develop automations.  Automations are subject to review before migration to Production, including a review of Privacy Thresholds and Security Review.  Each automation will not require a distinct Authority to Operate, but will be scrutinized appropriately.  All automations will be published to a Registry that will contain information to enable continued governance and monitoring.
Users of FRAME are expected to follow a Five-Phase process:
•	Select the Process
•	Diagram the Process
•	Diagram the Automation
•	Select the Tool
•	Develop the Automation
Even though it is not obvious from the wording, "Develop the Automation" is understood to include operation and maintenance of the automation.
UiPath and Blue Prism are commercial-off-the-shelf (COTS) offerings comprised of several software components.  The methodology and categorization (attended/un-attended) for reach product is in the following paragraphs.
UiPath
The FAA implementation of UiPath consists of the following three components:
•	Studio – A visual designer that allows authorized users to build automation workflows using pre-defined activities.
•	Robot – The automation workflows developed in UiPath Studio are executed by UiPath Robots.
•	Orchestrator – The core product; which is a "command-and-control" server where automations are published, licenses are served, activities are logged, and bots are managed.
UiPath offers both "Attended" and "Un-Attended" Robot Licenses.  UiPath attended bots are installed on a user's desktop, while un-attended bots require their own “virtual” desktop and are initiated by a schedule or other trigger.  Different run-time considerations are required for attended vs. un-attended, because a human operator cannot observe the execution of an un-attended bot in real-time (to detect if the bot encountered an unrecoverable error, for example).
Blue Prism
The approach that Blue Prism takes with automation is different from UiPath.  Blue Prism has one license offering: a "Digital Worker."  Blue Prism can emulate how other vendors perform attended automation (which they call "assisted automation"), but the cost for an attended UiPath bot license is about 90% less expensive than a Blue Prism Digital Worker license.
FRAME encourages and supports the use of Blue Prism only in un-attended scenarios.

name: Obstruction Evaluation / Airport Airspace Analysis
description:
The OE/AAA System provides the FAA, U.S. Department of Defense, U.S. Department of Homeland Security, state aviation, airport personnel and construction or alteration sponsors with one system through which data reporting and analyses are performed.  The OE/AAA System ensures the use of standardized procedures that expedite the collection, processing and distribution of this safety critical aeronautical information, while maintaining the integrity of the data collected and stored as records by the federal government.  The records produced from the OE/AAA System are permanently stored in the FAA Obstacle Authoritative Source (OAS) database where they are used by the FAA to maintain aeronautical charts, databases, products and services, as well as, to map manmade structures and/or airports deemed operationally significant to National Airspace System (NAS) operations or having landmark values.  

The OE/AAA web site enables individuals and organizations engaged in sponsoring construction and/or alteration projects both on location at airports and external to the airport periphery to easily notify the FAA of their intent and activities.  The OE/AAA website also provides tools and resources to the public to retrieve records processed by the FAA under these approved collection activities.  These records are also available for public consumption through other FAA Aeronautical Information Data products and services.

name: Duluth Display System
description:
The Duluth Display System (DDS) utilized at Duluth Air Traffic Control Tower is a website-based application which consolidates multiple operational references into one location. Most importantly is the Status Information Area which is a display of current operational data such as the latest official weather observation, active runways and approach in use, pertinent notices to airmen, equipment outages, and other local airport conditions.

To display this information, the Duluth Display System uses a website-based approach. A web server (ideally hosted in-house via the kiosk in the break room which already has a 5gb partition set aside for this project) transmits data over the internet to a web browser on the end-user’s device (an IPAD connected to the FAA network in this case). Additionally, the web server needs access to external data (publicly available government resources) to relay information regarding weather, traffic management, airspace notices, and so forth to the user in an easy to digest manner with minimal navigation or button clicks required. The end goal is to have this supplemental operational data available under one website.

Below are some of the features that our Web App provides:

● Weather
○ Surface observations (METAR) and terminal area forecasts (TAF),
weather radar (from National Weather Service and commercial providers),
hazardous weather information (AIRMETS / SIGMETS), 
○ the local weather forecast from National Weather Service
○ This information is presented either via hyperlink to the appropriate Government or Commercial website, or directly on screen via an XML request from the Text Data Server at aviationweather.gov

● Notices to airmen (NOTAMS)
○ Currently is linked to https://notams.aim.faa.gov/notamSearch/, however future development may utilize the SWIM / SWIFT Portal at https://www.faa.gov/air_traffic/technology/swim/, allowing a controller to easily view pertinent notams without leaving the primary DDS website.

● Temporary Flight Restrictions / Special Use Airspace
○ Currently provides a link to public FAA web pages displaying a graphical map of flight restrictions and active / pending special use airspace activations. Future development may utilize the SWIM / SWIFT portal (linked above) to present this data without leaving the primary DDS website.

● National Airspace System status
○ Displays the status of traffic flow management initiatives to common destination airports (ground stops, expect departure clearance times) and the general reason for flight delays.
○ This data is retrieved via “screen scraping” of the publicly available https://www.fly.faa.gov/flyfaa/plaintext.html website

● Charts and approach plates
○ Contains a listing of instrument approach plates at airports served by Duluth Tower, Duluth Approach, and pertinent surrounding airports which may require coordination between Duluth Approach and Minneapolis Center.
○ Charts are arranged first via selection of an airport, then sorted by the runway they serve, allowing any pertinent chart to be displayed on screen with 4 clicks or fewer. Alternatively, a controller would use an internet search for official charts, or manually flip through pages of a terminal procedures paper book.
○ The charts are hyperlinked directly to the https://aeronav.faa.gov/ file system, which is publicly available. Except MN33 (St. Mary’s Hospital Helipad) with three instrument procedures not available to the public, and will be stored on the display system web server as PDF files.

● Brief
○ PDF documents containing the position relief briefing checklists for the most commonly staffed operational positions in the tower and tracon.

name: National Offload Program 2.0
description:
The National Offload Program (NOP) is a system for the primary purpose of providing real-time and archived data via the FAA Intranet concerning the location and movement of aircraft flying within the United States National Airspace System (NAS). NOP 2.0 is a centralized Enterprise Information Management (EIM) cloud based system that transports data through the authorized System Wide Information Management (SWIM) security gateway. FAA authorized users access the data for the purposes of: Operational error detection, Airspace utilization and efficiency reports and studies, Traffic count, Air traffic controller training and Administrative tracking of time on position (Note: NOP only processes raw data utilized by downstream applications that create metadata in support of the above described initiatives).
NOP information is used within downstream FAA systems by Air Traffic Managers in the field for analysis of their airspace sector. The systems using the NOP information include FAA Headquarters personnel for statistical analysis of air traffic, local airport personnel for noise abatement and a myriad of other FAA organizations. This data is used to provide statistics related to flight plans, target tracks, and the business aspect of air traffic, which includes cost accounting, work productivity, traffic counts, resource management, etc.

name: Remote Monitoring and Logging System
description:
The Remote Monitoring and Logging System (RMLS) mission functions are Maintenance Management of all NAS systems and facilities and Monitor and control of selected remote NAS systems and facilities.

RMLS is the primary method used by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) to maintain the operation of NAS systems and facilities; the system improves the effectiveness of Tech Ops maintenance processes and practices and oversees the entire event management life cycle, from generation of the initial event through assignment, updates, and event closure. RMLS is comprised of two primary elements: (i) The National Logging Network (NLN) and (ii) The National Remote Maintenance Monitoring (RMM) Network (NRN).

The NLN component of RMLS provides enhanced management of the entire Logging Life Cycle from the generation of the initial event through assignment, update, and event closure. Logging tracks Preventive Events such as Periodic Maintenance and Certification, Corrective Events such as Facility and Service Outages, and Administrative Events such as aircraft incidents and flight inspections

The NRN component of RMLS is a NAS monitoring system, which provides the ability to monitor remotely the status of critical NAS facilities and operational equipment such as radars or navigational aids equipment. RMLS allows NAS technicians to determine quickly when a facility or equipment component or system is out of service resulting in an unscheduled outage. RMLS maintains an Emergency Contact list of Technicians to speed up equipment outage resolution. 

RMLS Maintenance information is used by the FAA to analyze trends and improve performance; to influence investment decisions and support budget requests for replacement, relocation, or modification of existing equipment; to detect supportability problems; to evaluate the efficiency and effectiveness of the overall maintenance program; and to provide reports to Congress and FAA management.

RMLS is composed of a suite of application: RMLS Simplified Automated Logging (SAL), Tech Ops Activities Portal (TAP), Operations Control Center (OCC) Event Manager (EM), National OCC (NOCC) EM, Maintenance Automation System Software (MASS), NAS Infrastructure Service (NIS), Peabody, Facility, Service and Equipment Profile (FSEP), National Airspace Performance Reporting System (NAPRS), Electronic Technical Performance Record (eTPR), Remote Maintenance Management Configuration & Administrative Tool (RMMCAT).

name: Aeronautical Information System Replacement
description: The AISR provides the automated means for collecting and distributing weather (Service A messages), flight plan data, NOTAM messages, Pilot Reports (PIREPS), and other operational information (Service B messages). This system allows general aviation and military users to file domestic/international aviation flight plans and to obtain weather data, NOTAMs, Pilot Reports (PIREPs), and other aeronautical information.  DoD users connect via NIPRNet, and FAA users connect via FTI-OPS. Military users can consolidate NOTAMs and flight-planning functions within a single AISR workstation (military users also use DINS to process NOTAMs). AISR is currently accessed at all FS-21 facilities, ARTCCs, and in approximately 100 ATCTs. At FS-21 facilities, AISR is also used as a back-up to the FS-21 system to enter and receive NOTAMs. AISR/SAM workstations are included in the asset inventory worksheet.

name: GNAS Equipment/Module Population
description:
The GEMPOP tool provides the national policy on standardizing Facility/ Service Equipment Profiles (FSEP) which governs the creation and maintenance of FSEP records. The records are stored in a national repository. Logs are maintained against these records to provide oversight of the facility's operational status. The automated logs from the Remote Monitoring and Logging System (RMLS) are used for analysis. These identify equipment performance and maintenance tends. In order for the automated logging and analysis to occur, certain RMLS tables must to populated and validated. These tables are Facility Equipment (FEQ), Facility Module (FMO), Periodic Maintenance Master (PMM), Periodic Maintenance Certification (PMC), Periodic Maintenance Task Glossary (PMT) and Equipment Type.
GEMPOP system functions are determined by authorization level. There are 3-primary functions provided in GEMPOP system.

1) The First function is a National function that will be used by AJW-1B. The data is provided from the technical instructions manuals (TIs) and Maintenance handbooks (MTHBs) in the National function.

2) The Second function is a Service Area function. This function will be the editing tool that would allow population, modification and validation of the tables within RMLS database for each facility type. Validation approval is given only to AJW-1B.

3) The Third primary function will analyze the corrective/ periodic maintenance, equipment modification and equipment modification and equipment/ module inventory data in RMLS. It provides performance statistics and trends for equipment and modules within the NAS.

name: NOTAM Entry System
description: The NOTAM Entry System (NES) is a web interface that allows users to create, review, and submit NOTAMs to the US NOTAM System (USNS) for distribution to the public. Critical NOTAMs, including Temporary Flight Restrictions (TFRs) are created and managed using NES, as all TFRs pass through NES for review by the US NOTAM Office (USNOF). Additionally, NES is used by the USNOF to view historical NOTAM data (including the FDC archive), view NADIN sent/receipt records,  create NOTAM templates for NES users and access USNOF daily logs. If NES is unable to function properly, the loss of these capabilities will have a significant impact on the safety of the NAS. The potential loss or delay in TFRs will be especially problematic.

name: Integrated Data Management System
description: The iDMS was developed to provide an automated solution for the maintenance and retrieval of project status information and related data, with the project number being the foundation in each area.  iDMS also provides a means to review online approved NAS related documentation and the processes for approving them.  The application has a component to enter the field support data for reporting and trend analysis.  Quality System Modifications are fielded with the preparation, tracking, and approvals handled within the application.  The applications provide a high degree of Configuration Management to these modifications and software updates.  The built in processes ensure each update is vetted against the current baseline, mitigating the chance of errors being released to the field.  The application provides a process to assist the documentation efforts in support of operational testing and evaluation of modifications on assigned equipment or software, and the readiness review of new systems.   The application provides a means to publish and issue the 6000 series directives known as the Maintenance Technical Handbook (MTHB).  This handbook contains the current agency approved maintenance standard, tolerances, schedules, and procedures.  As well, Technical Instruction Books (TIB) are updated and issued for the NAS Master Directory configuration management documents.  The authorizing documents for the MTHBs and TIBs are tracked, published, and issued through this application.

name: En Route Automation Modernization
description: En Route Automation Modernization (ERAM) is the primary Air Traffic Control Automation System used by air traffic controllers in the 20 Air Route Traffic Control Centers (ARTCC), with support and development systems located at the William J Hughes Technical Center (WJHTC) and Federal Aviation Administration Aeronautical Center (FAAAC). ERAM receives, processes and displays radar surveillance and flight data providing controllers with situational radar displays as well as tools and interfaces to interact with that data and each other. ERAM is a foundational program for NextGen.  ERAM offers an open software architecture, with modular sub-systems, that is easily enhanced to support the evolving operational needs of the National Airspace System (NAS). The ERAM architecture provides two highly available, full function channels which eliminates system down time due to scheduled and unscheduled outages and allows more flexibility for scheduled maintenance. The ERAM architecture provides separation of mission critical and non-mission critical functions and reduces air traffic control critical service outages. The ERAM infrastructure provides increased security to protect the En Route information assets.  The Airborne Reroute/Pre-Departure Reroute (ABRR/PDRR), Ground Interval Management Spacing (GIMS), DataComm S1P1 Terminal Services and DataComm S1P2 Initial Services Programs have already been integrated into ERAM.

name: United States NOTAM System
description:
USNS is the joint FAA/DoD system used for collecting, processing, maintaining, and distributing NOTAMs for the U.S. civilian and military aviation communities. The United States NOTAM Office (USNOF) is staffed by FAA US NOTAM specialists and military NOTAM coordinators that update the USNS.

A NOTAM provides information on temporary and/or immediate changes to the condition of any aeronautical facility, service, procedure, or component (e.g. runways, navigational aids, lighting) involved in flight operations. A NOTAM is originated when any authorized aviation specialist recognizes an event or condition that creates unsafe flying conditions. After identifying an unsafe condition, the process of getting the information into the NOTAM system depends on who has both the physical capability and logical authority to enter data.

name: NAS Support Infrastructure
description: The Terminal (AJM-24) and En Route and Oceanic (AJM-25) systems need to access NAS Operational (OPIP) sites from support environments at the William J. Hughes   Technical Center (WJHTC) to provide Second Level Engineering (SLE) support, including troubleshooting and file transfer (push/pull data). Up to this point, each AJM-24/25 program has implemented its own strategy for accessing OPIP systems, including one-off NESG integration and legacy direct OPIP connections from the support environments connected to the Mission Support (MS) network.  This has resulted in increased costs, duplication of efforts, and security concerns. To alleviate these issues, AJM-25 has implemented a virtual infrastructure solution to expedite and standardize Terminal and En Route & Oceanic systems integration with the NAS Enterprise Security Gateway (NESG).  The infrastructure consists of physical servers (virtualization infrastructure), virtual servers (VMs), routers, and storage.  This managed demilitarized zone (DMZ) solution, the NSI, provides boundary protection between the support environments at the WJHTC and NAS OpIP for machine-to-machine data flows. AJM-24/25 systems are allowed to onboard to this environment.

name: AJM-25 Operational Support Environment
description:
The AJM-25 Operational Support Environment (OSE) is a non-National Airspace System (NAS) General Support System (GSS). As an independent, yet highly interconnected network environment, the AJM-25 OSE contains or connects a variety of important assets, including system software development environments, problem tracking and reporting tools, and system laboratories. The AJM-25 OSE maintains critical functions, such as real-time site support, and it provides remote access to mission critical applications.
The AJM-25 OSE is located inside the laboratory environment at the WJHTC, Atlantic City, NJ. Most of the hardware and networking equipment for the OSE, including System Administrators’ PCs and the Development Servers (used for building packages for ERAM or for accessing site support), are housed in the En Route and Oceanic NAS Support Environment (EONSE) portion of the lab (located in Bldg. 300). Specialty Engineering, AJM-2512, provides the network support services, including Domain Name System (DNS), Password Manager Pro (PMP), Mail Relay, Syslog, and Web Services, to the AJM-25 OSE from within the EONSE.
The AJM-25 OSE provides operational support to the lab environments for the following NAS and non-NAS Systems:
•	Advanced Technologies & Oceanic Procedures (ATOP)
•	Display System Replacement (DSR)
•	En Route Communications Gateway (ECG)/ Enhanced Back Up Surveillance (EBUS)/RAPPI
•	En Route Automation Modernization (ERAM)
•	En Route Information Display System (ERIDS)
•	Integrated Display System Replacement (IDSR)/NAS Information Display System (NIDS)
•	Integration and Interoperability Facility (IIF) Network (supports ATOP and ERAM)
•	Microprocessor En Route Automated Radar Tracking System (MEARTS or Micro-EARTS)
•	Offshore Flight Data Processing System (OFDPS)
•	Oceanic Integration and Interoperability Facility (OIIF) (supports ATOP) 
•	Simulation Driver and Radar Recorder (SDRR)
•	Time Based Flow Management (TBFM)
•	Terrestrial EnRoute Radar Analysis (TERRA)/Distributed Radar Analysis and Monitoring System 2 (DRAMS 2)

name: Defense Internet NOTAM Service
description:
DINS provides real-time NOTAMs to DoD NIPRNet and Internet users. DINS is primarily for DoD aircrews to retrieve NOTAMs and for authorized DoD Military Based Operations (MBO) personnel to process (create, cancel, and replace) military NOTAMs. DINS interfaces with the USNS. The DINS database is replicated in near real-time with USNS. The user interface for DINS is a web portal for NOTAM retrieval and entry. Newly created military NOTAMs are transmitted using Transport Layer Security (TLS) over secure hypertext transfer protocol (HTTPS) via the military’s NIPRNet or the Internet to the DINS server.

The DINS System has associated applications that provide web-based query services that include:

• DINS Create and Cancel/Replace (CCR) is a graphical NOTAM tool that enhances safety by assisting pilots in identifying areas that are closed or under construction. DINS CCR also uses USNS Web Service to submit NOTAMs.
• DINS Query is primarily limited to querying by issuing location, and this is primarily used to find NOTAMs for the Departure and Destination International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) codes only. ICAO codes are four-letter identifier codes that uniquely identify individual airports worldwide.

name: Special Use Airspace Management System
description: SAMS is the system of record for all Special Use Airspace (SUA) activity within the National Airspace System (NAS), per FAA Order JO 7610.4. SAMS automates the coordination of FAA and United States (U.S.) DoD scheduling of SUA and other special activity areas. SAMS collects airspace schedule requests from military and other agencies, ensures that the appropriate FAA controlling center is aware and approves of the planned airspace usage and corresponding safety restrictions for the flying public, and disseminates this information to pilots and planners affected by SUA restrictions and other special-purpose operations. Among other functions, SAMS provides the capability for users to create, store, and retrieve airspace activity schedule information from the underlying Consolidated Special Use Airspace Repository (CSAR) database.

name: Air Route Traffic Control Center Critical Essential Power System Power Monitoring System
fullname_0: Air Route Traffic Control Center Critical Essential Power System Power Monitoring System
description:
A monitoring system is being installed at all FAA Air Route Traffic Control Center (ARTCC) sites that will allow detailed observation of the ACEPS.  The purpose of the APMS is to intelligently monitor and graphically display power system health, status, and performance. Using the combination of sophisticated monitoring hardware and real-time analysis software, the system provides to users the following capabilities:

• Access to real-time displays and historical trending of energy and quality parameters 
• Capture electrical events and anomalies 
• Provide reporting on facility system status 
• Perform comprehensive root cause analysis of past events 
• Provide expert recommendations on system alignment, reconfigurations, and maintenance due to system performance, updates, and the facilities operational picture 
• Develop and implement effective predictive maintenance procedures

name: ADS-B Service Assurance System
description:
ASAS will aid a user in detecting and locating radio frequency (RF) interference to both the Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS B) and the Global Positioning System (GPS)/Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) spectrum. ASAS will also indicate near real-time surveillance spectrum usage.

The implementation of ASAS will:
• Provide SBS systems engineering, FAA spectrum management, AT and technical operations personnel with Radio Frequency Interference (RFI) source identification and location tools
• Support air traffic operations during SBS service degradation due to equipment or service outages resulting from jamming or spoofing events
• Provide the situational awareness to support actions that may be taken by command center, operations control centers and other organizations charged with spectrum management and protection, for the purposes of identification, location and suppression or cessation of interference sources
• Support surveillance spectrum usage analysis, including development of historical usage patterns to aid in identificaiton of aberrant or unusual spectrum activity that may be indicative of jamming or spoofing.
• Support anlaysis of Department of Defense (DoD) testing events that have the potential to impact NAS surveillance spectrum.

fullname_0: ESC Middle-Tier and Enterprise Support Applications
description: ESC Middle Tier and Enterprise Support Applications (EMTESA) is comprised of middle tier and enterprise applications located in the ESC Enterprise Data Center (ESC-EDC) at the Mike Monroney Aeronautical Center in Oklahoma City, OK as well as the disaster recovery/backup site at the U.S. Department of Agriculture’s Digital Infrastructure Services Center (DISC) in Kansas City, Missouri. fullname_0: National Airspace System Aeronautical Information Management Enterprise System
description:
NAIMES is a National Airspace System (NAS) mission support program managed by the Air Traffic Organization (ATO) System Operations Services and Aeronautical Information Management AJW. NAIMES provides customers and stakeholders with “one-stop” access to critical Aeronautical Information (AI) products and services. The NAIMES mission is to process and distribute AI to the FAA, DoD, and commercial air carrier and general aviation customers in support of Air Traffic Control (ATC) operations. NAIMES supports the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) mission to promote aviation safety, security, and performance.
NAIMES is a FAA Safety of Flight/Mission Essential system and a Department of Defense (DoD) Mission Critical system. The NAIMES program is the authoritative source for Notices to Airmen (NOTAM) messages and AI System Replacement (AISR) system data for NAS users. The NAIMES system consists of multiple, closely integrated systems and services that support the collection, validation, management and dissemination of AI.
The NAIMES system collects NOTAM messages and AI from the National Airspace Data Interchange Network (NADIN). NAIMES also collects, processes and distributes flight plans and weather data by way of the FAA’s FTI Operational Network (FTI-OPS), the FAA Mission Support Network, the DoD NIPRNet and Internet sources. NAIMES provides AI portal capabilities and data distribution to various locations, systems, and networks.

name: National Airspace System Resources
description:
National Airspace System Resource (NASR) is the official database repository for NAS aeronautical data, including Airspace resources and FAA facilities used by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). NASR and its predecessor (Aeronautical Information System – GIM II) have been supplying aeronautical data to internal FAA aviation customers for more than 30 years.  NASR is the primary source for U.S. aeronautical data for FAA internal and external aviation authorities and third-party data providers. NASR consists of fixed aeronautical information (airports, runways, navigational aids, instrument landing systems, fixes, airways, military training routes, towers, and the remaining fixed assets of the NAS) and theoretical entities (routes, navigational facilities and ARTCC boundaries etc.).
 
NASR provides capabilities to manage the collection, validation, storage, maintenance, and dissemination of static aeronautical data for the National Airspace System (NAS).  NASR manages a database of aeronautical data and manages message traffic to report temporary and permanent changes to facilities in the NAS. These services are essential to air traffic operations and support various FAA programs and other US Government functions.

name: FAA DroneZone - Notice of Identification
description:
The Notice of Identification is a service in the FAA DroneZone that will allow an account owner to create a Notice of Identification update the NOI, add aircraft/drone inventory and create a Confirmation of Identification as required by part 89 for operators of aircraft/drones that are registered in a foreign country.
•	The Part 89 Remote Identification (RID) rule includes a unique requirement for persons operating foreign registered civil Unmanned Aircraft (UA) with remote identification in the airspace of the United States. This requirement (§89.130 Confirmation of Identification) states that an operator of a foreign registered civil UA with RID must, prior to operating, submit a Notice of Identification to the FAA and obtain a Confirmation of Identification. Further, the operator must update the information in the notice as applicable prior to operating.

name: License Electronic Application Portal
description:
LEAP will allow the FAA Office of Commercial Space Transportation (AST) to automate the intake and processing of commercial space license applications.

Background: The Office of Commercial Space Transportation (AST) was established in 1984 (Commercial Space Launch Act of 1984, as amended and re-codified at 51 U.S.C. 50901 – 50923) as part of the Office of the Secretary of Transportation within the Department of Transportation (DOT). In November 1995, Commercial Space Transportation was transferred to the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) as the FAA's only space-related line of business. Among its duties, AST was established to regulate the U.S. commercial space transportation industry, ensure compliance with international obligations of the United States, and protect the public health and safety, property safety, and national security and foreign policy interests of the United States.

AST issued the first commercial launch license in 1989 when a Starfire sub-orbital vehicle carried aloft the Consort-1 payload from White Sands Missile Range in New Mexico. AST, now in the FAA, issued its first commercial human space flight license on April 1, 2004, to Scaled Composites for the launch of Space Ship One (SS1). The SS1 program was the first private commercial human space flight program.

Commercial Space License application processing has been successful in the past, using procedures and processes that were adequate at the time but may not be sustainable due to current and future industry growth. The current methodology is not conducive to scalability, traceability, and consistency. Current reliance upon shared drives and email is fraught with issues such as losing emails, stripping of attachments, file size limitations, and accessibility. The current process for referencing prior application materials and evaluations over many modifications and renewals makes it difficult to capture the complete approved application and evaluation.

name: SAE Mobilus / ARINC
description:
Must be accessed from the Consensus Standards Access SharePoint Site in order to get to FAA subscription: https://ksn2.faa.gov/ajw/es4/nes/res/SitePages/Consensus_Standards.aspx

SAE is a standards development organization that develops and publishes voluntary consensus standards.  Principal emphasis is placed on global transport industries such as aerospace, automotive, and commercial vehicles. The FAA subscription includes electronic downloads to SAE standards made available through SAE Mobilus.

name: FrontPage II
description:
The FrontPage2 (FP2) is an FAA owned SQL Server based application used to automate, retain and distribute existing and proposed Instrument Flight Procedures (IFP) data to the obstacle impact screening tools such as eTERPS and FLOAT. FP2 is the only source for proposed instrument procedure data. 

Functionality- Instrument Flight Procedure Data repository and distribution application. 

Business Purpose- Support the 14 CFR Part 77, Safe, efficient use and preservation of the Navigable Airspace by retaining automated information regarding existing and proposed Instrument Flight Procedure data gathered by IFP Specialists from numerous automated and non-automated sources. The data retained in the FP2 is distributed to obstacle screening tools to assist the Obstacle Impact Team specialists in protecting the navigable airspace from over 150K obstacles proposed each year.

name: Parking and Transit Benefits System
description:
The Parking and Transit Benefit System (PTBS) is the Department of Transportation (DOT) Information Technology system used to manage the Federal Transit Benefit Program (FTBP) and facilitate the distribution of public-transportation funding. PTBS incorporates the system formerly known as Headquarters Parking Application (HPA).

On April 21, 2000 Executive Order (EO) 13150, Federal Workforce Transportation, was issued to reduce Federal employees’ contributions to traffic congestion and air pollution in the National Capitol Region (NCR) by increasing the attractiveness of mass transit with full tax-free benefits and vanpool options. In order to promote the use of mass transportation on a national basis, DOT implemented the FTBP for Federal Agencies in the NCR and nationwide. The NCR is defined as the District of Columbia; Montgomery, Prince George's, and Frederick Counties in Maryland; Arlington, Fairfax, Loudon, and Prince William Counties in Virginia.  The benefits has since changed to providing transit benefit funding to Federal Government employees who have been approved for this benefit.

Within DOT’s Office of the Assistant Secretary for Administration, the Office of Transportation Services (TRANServe) provides transit benefit support services to DOT and other federal agencies nationwide through PTBS.  Services include providing timely and efficient transit benefit services to over 150,000 customers.

name: Proxy Offload Program
description:
Proxy Offload Program (POP) is a new system, supported by ACG funding, that will replace NOP and will provide:

○ Secured transmission with guaranteed delivery of raw NAS data to FAA AIT Cloud Services (EIM) for distribution to non-NAS consumers on the FAA Mission Support (MS) Network.  POP solution leverages enterprise services for boundary protection and secure data transmission.  POP is compliant with Order 1370.121B, FAA Information Security and Privacy and Order 1370.114, Implementation of FAA Telecommunication Infrastructure Services and IS Requirements in the NAS.  This solution addresses missing System Wide Information Management (SWIM) data until SWIM R6.1 capability is ready in 2025 (deployment complete in FY26) upon which the POP solution will be decommissioned.

○ Plan of Action and Milestone (POAM) remediation funding kicked off POP, a stop-gap solution created to remediate NOP.

name: Laboratory Capabilities Tool
description:
LCT is an information system that provides a web interface for laboratory owners/manager (LCT administrative/standard users) to catalogue their FAA aviation laboratories’ contact information and capabilities into a database. LCT’s purpose is to eliminate the duplication of hardware, software and personnel resources by allowing authenticated users to search for and discover preexistent laboratory assets that may possibly be shared across FAA locations, departments and divisions. name: Environmental Prescreening Filter Tool
description:
The Instrument Flight Procedures EPFT (also called the “Filter Tool”) is a web application designed to allow procedure designers, airport personnel, and Environmental Protection Specialists (EPSs) an easy and efficient way to share information when requesting a new or amended procedure. The tool contains logic that provides either a recommendation for the action to be categorically excluded from further environmental review, or to be sent to the Environmental Specialist for further review. The procedure designer and airport contact provide information needed to process the request, and the environmental specialist uses this information to determine if the procedure request is eligible for a Categorical Exclusion (CATEX) or if additional review or screening is required before a determination is made. 
The purpose of the filter tool is to streamline the process of environmental review for smaller-scale, new or amended IFP designs. The tool provides an interface for passing information between the procedure designer, the airport, and the environmental specialist, reduces manual back-and-forth communication, and provides a place for all information about a proposed procedure to be stored in one location.

name: Sector Design and Analysis Tool
description:
SDAT is a Federal Aviation Administration (FAA)-owned system that provides users with a web-enabled application for creating, analyzing, processing, and validating Minimum Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) Altitude (MIA) and Minimum Vector Altitude (MVA) charts, and Sector Designated Airspace (SDA) and Terminal Radar Approach Control (TRACON) Designated Airspace (TDA) projects.

SDAT is used by facilities throughout the National Airspace System (NAS) for full-scale airspace redesign projects that include evaluation of obstacle impacts on flight procedures, airspace design and documentation, sector analysis and data translation, sector metrics and traffic visualization, and automation support. In accordance with FAA Order 7210.3, SDAT produces, saves, and stores each airspace project, including all pertinent documentation required or used for the chart or project submittal, as well as all validation process approvals.

As the lead federal government agency responsible for regulating and providing safety oversight of commercial motor vehicles (CMVs), FMCSA's mission is to reduce crashes, injuries, and fatalities involving large trucks and buses.

FMCSA partners with industry, safety advocates, and state and local governments to keep our nation's roadways safe and improve CMV safety through regulation, education, enforcement, research, and technology.

name: RedHat OpenShift on AWS
description:
ROSA is a fully-managed, turnkey application platform that allows you to focus on delivering value to your customers by building and deploying applications. Red Hat site reliability engineering (SRE) experts manage the underlying platform so you do not have to worry about the complexity of infrastructure management. ROSA provides seamless integration with a wide range of AWS compute, database, analytics, machine learning, networking, mobile, and other services to further accelerate the building and delivering of differentiating experiences to your customers. 
You subscribe to the service directly from your AWS account. After the clusters are created, you can operate your clusters with the OpenShift web console or through Red Hat OpenShift Cluster Manager. The ROSA service also uses OpenShift APIs and command-line interface (CLI) tools. These tools provide a standardized OpenShift experience to use your existing skills and tools knowledge. 
You receive OpenShift updates with new feature releases and a shared, common source for alignment with OpenShift Container Platform. ROSA supports the same versions of OpenShift as Red Hat OpenShift Dedicated and OpenShift Container Platform to achieve version consistency.

name: UAS Services - Common Authentication Service
description:
The Common Authentication Service (CAS) is a service that is intended to authenticate service providers and consumers of FAA services that exchange UAS data among its users.
CAS is designed such that when a consumer wants to access LAANC and GDFS endpoints, an Access Token is requested and generated. The client must request an access token with a proper set of scopes mapped to an audience that data-providing service accounts are configured to support.
CAS deployed REST APIs that are used to provide authentication services (tokens to support consumer REST API execution). The first consumer of this application was LAANC, facilitating the effort to transition LAANC USSs from their current authentication process. USS retrieve tokens through CAS, and then use those tokens in LAANC-USS and GDFS REST API calls. LAANC O&M Checker will also retrieve tokens from CAS.

name: Emergency Operations Network - ArcGIS Online
description:
The FAA WOC has a responsibility[1] to maintain detailed knowledge of the NAS and to share critical information with the FAA Administrator, Senior FAA Leadership and external organizations or agencies about incidents affecting the safety and security of NAS such as drone sightings and/or incidents involving the use of lasers pointed at aircrafts in restricted/controlled airspace. To address requirements for sharing visual data with external organizations, the FAA turned to and purchased Esri ArcGIS cloud services. Through this purchase the EON Program leverages the AGO cloud service. This cloud service enables the FAA WOC to share critical information with external organizations or agencies for the purpose of promoting and maintaining public safety and security of navigable airspace by civil aircraft in the NAS. In certain instances, external organizations or agencies will request specific NAS incident data or submit an RFI to the FAA WOC for drone sightings and/or incidents involving the use of lasers pointed at aircraft(s) in restricted or controlled airspace. The purpose of these requests are to support law enforcement initiatives when implementing mitigation to maintain public safety and security of the NAS during special and high profile events (e.g., G-7 Summit at Camp David, Presidential Inaugurations, Super Bowl, and other events). Other purposes in responding to the RFIs include:

WOC ability to maintain effective communication and exchange of information with those who have a need to know (other federal/state/local government agencies) during emergencies.  WOC ability to share critical information with external organizations or agencies to maintain situational awareness and maintain a common operational picture of relevant information about UAS and incidents involving the use of lasers pointed at aircrafts in restricted/controlled airspace.
[1] Responding to RFIs and sharing critical information with external organizations/agencies with a need to know enables the FAA WOC to follow and comply with statutory regulations defined in 49 USC 40101; 49 USC 40103; and Public Law 112-95 Section 333 commensurate with maintaining and enhancing safety and security of navigable airspace by civil aircraft in the NAS.

name: Florida Test Bed
description:
The Florida Test Bed (FTB) is a state-of-the-art 10,000-plus-foot facility conveniently and strategically located adjacent to Daytona Beach International Airport and near Embry-Riddle Aeronautical University (ERAU). ERAU NextGen Programs are conducted at Florida Test Bed, an agile research and integration facility designed to allow government, industry, and academia to showcase their ideas and technologies in a NextGen National Airspace System (NAS) environment.
FTB consists of two (2) primary areas — the Demonstration Suite and the Integration Suite — plus a Data Center that houses the network equipment, rack-mounted servers, and other 
equipment required to drive the operational capabilities in the Integration and Demonstration Suites. FTB provides a platform for new NextGen demonstrations to be conducted at an early stage without affecting NAS operations. This enables the ability to integrate individual domains to allow multi-domain, end-to-end NextGen demonstrations and evaluations. FTB core infrastructure is architected and configured to enable remote connections with other Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) NextGen and industry partner sites to allow for multi-site demonstration capabilities and NAS based modeling and simulation. This approach reduces risk and overall costs by enabling the FAA to evaluate the viability of these new technologies and concepts before making further investments and decisions on potential implementation in operations. 
In addition, FTB allows the integration of new and emerging technologies or applications into existing or planned NAS enhancements, while fostering government partnerships. FTB provides an environment that allows open access for industry users, academia, and vendors. Through its governance framework, FTB provides the ability for industry to bring and integrate new concepts and technologies, maintain and sustain their systems at FTB, and conduct ongoing activities. This unique approach promotes innovation from industry, encourages in-kind contributions and R&D investment, and leverages industry’s capabilities to provide realistic solutions to the FAA and help evaluate NextGen concepts. The demonstrations supported within FTB are envisioned to facilitate development and implementation of emerging NextGen technologies. 
FTB provides an environment that allows for the integration of prototypes to demonstrate and evaluate arising NextGen technologies. Through a test bed governance model, FAA, industry, academia, airline partners, other government agencies, and international aviation organizations can gain regulated access to FTB infrastructure. FTB supports NextGen activities by: Acting as a platform to conduct NextGen technology and concept evaluations and demonstrations. Allowing FAA to understand prospects of the early-stage concept or technology for implementation and understand potential benefits and risks. Helping FAA make decisions on potential operational implementation. In order to support NextGen concept demonstration activities, FTB provides a suite of NAS systems in a prototype environment that includes the current version of the systems with modifications incorporated from previous demonstrations. While this environment is completely separate from the operational environment, updates to the systems in the operational environment can be reflected into FTB environment, and new NextGen concepts demonstrated at FTB have the potential for being incorporated for implementation in the future.

name: Civil Aviation Registry Applications
description:
AVS Registry is a large, multi-faceted system that acts as the legal repository of both aircraft and airmen (pilots, aircraft mechanics, etc.) records.  The system is comprised of multiple component subsystems, servicing either airmen or aircraft.  The systems and subsystems are as follow:
•	Registry Modernization System (RMS)
      o	Airmen Document Control System (AADOCS)
      o	Comprehensive Airmen Information System (CAIS)
      o	Aircraft Document Control System (ARDOCS)
      o	Aircraft Registration System (AR)
      o	Image Management System (IMS)
      o	Registry Forms System
•	Electronic Document Retrieval System II (EDRS II)
•	Registry Web Server
RMS includes imaging and workflow subsystems, which have enhanced the ability to maintain airmen and aircraft records.  RMS is the key link that acts as a collection of applications spanning the EASE Mainframe and all other AVS Registry components.
The Airmen Certification Branch, AFB-720, is responsible for the issuance of all permanent FAA airmen certificates, the content of all airmen certification records, and law enforcement assistance as it involves the airmen certification program.  AVS Registry serves as the national repository for airmen certification records and provides the central services necessary for control of these records, which are used in court litigation, employment, and insurance verification by the aviation industry.  Airmen data contains Social Security Numbers (SSN), dates of birth (DOB), and other information that is considered Personally Identifiable Information (PII).  The EASE Mainframe-based CAIS maintains these records.  Examiners review applications for certification and issue certificates to airmen on a daily basis.
The Aircraft Registry Branch, AFB-710, is responsible for the national programs of aircraft registration, recording of encumbrances against U.S. civil aircraft, identification of registered aircraft, and law enforcement assistance as it involves the aircraft registration program.  AVS Registry serves as the national repository for aircraft records containing registration, lien, and airworthiness information.  Registering aircraft results in the issuance of a certificate and the assignment of U.S. registration markings (N-Numbers or tail numbers).  Aviation Registry system provides automated support in accomplishing these tasks and in providing detailed information about the U.S. civil aircraft fleet.  In general, the system contains a detailed description of the aircraft as well as the name and address of the registered owner.

name: Managed Print Output
description:
Lexmark Document Distributor (LDD) print processing software controlling the fleet of ~650 Multifunctional Devices (MFDs) providing an enterprise print, scan, fax, and copy functionality to the FAA.

MPO utilizes the Lexmark Print Management (LPM) software utility. The goal and mission of the MPO is to provide convenient, reliable, secure, and cost-effective printing services to FAA personnel. To modernize the FAA's printer inventory, optimize how employees use printers, and reduce the escalating total cost to the agency. The MPO features multi-functional devices that can print, copy, scan, and in many cases fax, create a one-stop-shop for personnel, and replace numerous devices cluttering valuable workspace. It has a convenient feature known as the “follow-me” feature where personnel send print jobs from their computer to any Managed Print device in any FAA facility, and securely retrieve it with their PIV card at any point within 72 hours of submission. The print jobs are sent and stored in the system queue for 72 hours on the FAA’s Isilon File Storage arrays. There is an additional 8-hour hold time for job re-print. Once the job is printed or the set storage time has expired, the print job is deleted from the system.

name: Internal Substance Abuse Program
description:
The DOT oversees FAA's Internal Substance Abuse Program (ISAP). The program is designed to randomly test Testing Designated Positions (TDP) FAA employees who occupy agency positions designated as having safety- and/or security-related duties. In addition, all agency employees are subject to post-accident, reasonable suspicion, and follow-up drug testing.  Applicants for a safety or security related TDP are subject to pre-employment testing.  Non-TDP employees transferring into a TDP are subject to pre-appointment testing.  TDP employees on a Treatment and Rehabilitation Program (TRP) must have a Return-to-Duty (RTD) test and placed into a follow-up testing program for a minimum of 365 days.  Non-TDP employees are not subjected to a RTD before being placed into a follow-up testing program for a minimum of 365 days.

name: ILS Continuity of Service Analysis System
fullname_0: ILS Continuity of Service Analysis System
description:
CoS (Continuity of Service) is a term commonly used to refer to a suite of programs that are used in the implementation of FAA Order 6750.57.  This order was created around 2007 to help the FAA prove compliance of Category II/III Instrument Landing Systems with ICAO requirements.  ICAO (International Civil Aviation Organization) is an agency of the United Nations that imposes aviation requirements on the UN’s member states.
The specific requirement addressed by CoS is the probability that an ILS being used to land an airplane will remain operational for the duration of an aircraft approach operation.  The probability is required to be extremely high, and the accepted proof is maintaining a very high MTBO (mean time between outage).
Tracking MTBO by hand would be extremely labor intensive and prone to error or manipulation.  To ensure consistency, an automated process was created and first released to widespread FAA usage in 2008.
The CoS process makes use of a number of different software programs.  Some were already existing within the FAA.  Others were specifically created for CoS.
Since the early 2000s, the FAA has had an automated event reporting system.  When equipment outages occur, an LIR (Log Interruption Record) is created in a database.  There is another database called FSEP (Facility Service and Equipment Profile) which lists all equipment installed within the NAS (National Airspace).  These two existing databases provide the core data used to compute and track MTBO.
CoS specific software is composed of two main programs and a number of utilities.
One of the two main programs is “CoS Update”.  This program runs on a server at MMAC.  Once a day, it queries another server which resides at FAA Headquarters and gathers FSEP and LIR data.  The server at FAA HQ is running Microsoft SQL Server.  The “CoS Update” program is a Windows console program that is written in C++.  “CoS Update” makes several SQL queries using an ODBC link to the FAA HQ server.  It stores all the data retrieved and then post-processes the data into a CoS specific format.
The other main program is “CoS Analyze”.  This is a native Windows desktop client application, also written in C++.  This program downloads the post-processed CoS specific data from the MMAC server and computes MTBO using the algorithm defined in FAA Order 6750.57.  Computation of MTBO is not entirely automated.  There is a human element involved.  Some outages can be correlated to the same event, or in other words multiple outages with the same underlying cause can be counted as a single outage.  There are a small number of equipment specialists called OPRs, just a couple for each Service Area, who make the determination for how outages can be correlated.  When a change is made, the OPR enters the change into his or her copy of “CoS Analyze”.  The change can then be uploaded to the MMAC server for distribution to the entire CoS community.  The upload is a password protected operation that sends the data from “CoS Analyze” to a Perl script running on the MMAC Apache server.  The Perl script is one of the CoS utilities mentioned above, and resides in the directory “CoS Put”.

name: Business Intelligence Server
description:
Functionally, this server does the following major services:
*LEAVE TRACKER : It provides leave information to ALL employees of ALL FAA centers (ALL US Mainland centers plus off shore centers – ZAN (Anchorage), ZUA (Guam), and ZSU (San Juan))
*ESIS (Enhanced Status Information System) – displays critical operational data on ALL areas of ZOA control room floor, including MOS.
*Provides up-to-the-minute, operational data to management staff of ALL centers – like TOP (Time on Position), OJT (On the Job Training), OT (Over Time), Sector view to show who is/was at what position on floor for selected date by user, etc. This just a short list.
*The server has quite a few automated management reports (summarizing operational data), going out daily or Weekly. It uses SQL Server BI (Business Intelligence Tool) which can fetch data from any type of database (Oracle database of CruX is the main one) but it integrates diverse type of data sources like SQL Server, Excel workbooks, Access database, etc.
supportedbyfaatechnologystandards: Microsoft SQL Server 2012 Standard, Enterprise (EOL); Microsoft Windows Server 2019  (Contained)
technologyremediationactivity_0:
03/25/2025; Microsoft SQL Server 2012 Standard, Enterprise; Tech refresh planned; 3/25/2025 - Per working session with PoC:  We are working to move this solution to the Cloud and remove the On-prem server.

9/17/2024 - This solution was identified as Noncompliant during the September Noncompliant solution escalation process.  Email send to Rohitjumar Desai and Michael A Galvan for awareness and remediation planning.  R, Desai responded:  I must admit that the non-compliance listed is accurate. However, since the system has to be eventually migrated to cloud, there is no reason for now to invest in SQL server upgrade- which is quite expensive, with the cost almost in lines with the hardware costs of the new server. All components of SQL server 2016 were obtained from Microsoft and were merged to make SQL server 2012 work with Windows Server 2019 operating system. The SQL server is only a backend database and has moderate use of BI data - not heavily used. As such, the only component of SQL Server named DTS (Data Transformation Services, which has been part of SQL server since almost 2000 ) is the most heavily used for automation for gathering data from diverse data sources, perform ETL (Extraction, Transformation and Loading), and then disseminate reports to the management at some frequency (daily, Weekly or Monthly) automatically. The server’s main function on the other hand, is to provides access to LEAVE data to ALL employees of ALL centers, up-to-minute operational data to management of ALL centers and the most importantly ESIS (Enhanced Status Information System) to the control room floor. The Server hardware and Operating system were upgraded - It runs with modern/latest hardware (like all SD memory, good strength processors, etc.) and uses Windows Server 2019 and provides industry standard of less than 3 seconds response to all users. It works flawlessly! Not sure where exactly we fall in budget process (will let Michael Galvan respond to it) but thing I know is: All FAA servers which has database at backend were delayed for migration to cloud last. I looked for a test space in cloud, especially to test response time for ESIS to compare it against the current server response which is on the same network as control room floor but even that I am unable to get.

6/24/24 - Per POC:  There is no funding available to upgrade, we are considering moving to Cloud but that also has associated costs.

name: Aeronautical Data Delivery Service
description:
This is a public-facing website managed by the FAA that lives outside of the FAA network.  It utilizes the COTS Esri ArcGIS Online platform, and therefore is not a custom applications.  The ArcGIS Online platform is a service that allows customers to publish data online, at which point that data is stored on Esri’s cloud infrastructure, and is then made available to the public to view, download, and utilize via web services. All data published to ADDS is data that is suitable and intended for public release, with most of the data already publicly available in other formats.  There is no operational data on either site – it is all static aeronautical information – mostly derived from the FAA aeronautical charts and publications managed by Aeronautical Information Services.

There are no direct connections by any FAA applications. The UASFM system posts data nightly to UDDS via a scripted publishing job, but there are no back-end database connections whatsoever.  All applications that utilize data from ADDS are either downloading that data or utilizing the web services.
This solution is used widely in the UAS applications of UASFM, LAANC, FAADroneZone (and it’s subsystems) and B4UFLY.

name: Smart Facility Telemetry Server VM
description:
The Smart Facility Program expands Technical Operations Remote Maintenance Monitoring (RMM) capabilities, enabling greater remote monitoring and automation, condition-based maintenance, and the opportunity for a data driven predictive maintenance program.

New sensory technology is added and retrofitted on existing non-RMM NAS systems and infrastructure to measure system operating conditions such as temperature inside equipment cabinets, vibration of air handlers, and battery voltage and charge status. Existing RMM-enabled NAS system data pipelines are optimized and extended with new and additional RMM logical unit identifiers (LUIDs) and new sensor technology installed to generate new information.

The local on-premises server, Local Ignition Server, receives and captures serial-over-IP sensory data and data from other local systems and infrastructure monitoring sources, and allows local monitor and control (M&C) functions of each of the sensors (smart building). The Local Ignition Server subscribes and blends RMM data with the local sensory data to help identify anomalies in the system performance and to gather timely and accurate insights to improve efficiency of performing maintenance. Integrated data dashboards and mobile tools provide more data to help technical field teams perform data-driven tasks remotely such as system health checks, technical performance reports (TPR) and support system diagnosis with real-time and predictive analytics.

In the planning phases is collecting the data at the EIM data lake to apply advanced data analytics and Reliability Centered Maintenance (RCM) techniques to allow development of integrated dashboards for more informed investment decisions.

description: There are two main solutions used on this server. The first is Subversion (SVN) which is a version control or configuration control system. These files include things such as interface control documents, system and software design files, software source code, system drawing files, and test reports. The second solution or application used on this server is Bugzilla. name: Rotor Manufacturing Lessons Learned Database
description:
The Aerospace Industries Association (AIA) and the FAA formed the Rotor Manufacturing (RoMan) 
project consisting of aircraft engine OEMs whose charter was to establish industry guidelines that improve manufacturing, engineering, and quality practices towards eliminating manufacturing induced anomalies in critical rotating parts.  To proactively address hazardous engine effects, the industry was asked to develop an industry wide Lessons Learned data sharing process.  This data sharing process was formalized and accepted by the rotor manufacturing (RoMan) team in October 1999.
To facilitate the process of data sharing the FAA issued a notice of proposed non-disclosure under the provisions of FAR 193 (Protection of Voluntarily Submitted Information).  An essential part of the FAR 193 rule was the requirement that the database be maintained separately by an independent third-party organization.
The LLDB website application developed using Microsoft Internet Information Server/Active Server Pages platform supports the LLDB users in anonymously sharing incident data and lessons learned, examining/reviewing the Common Lessons Learned Database records, asking and responding with clarification comments to enhance data quality, reviewing incident trends, and performing various data analysis tasks.
OEMs cite the AIA RoMan team lessons learned sharing activity as being a positive driver for manufacturing process improvements such as automation to minimize manual (human) operations and process monitoring implementation (either in production or as part of ongoing evaluations).
Data analysis has led to an improved understanding of the underlying controls necessary to define the manufacturing method capability especially in the areas of tool design, condition control, and quality.   For example, the AIA RISC has used the RoMan LLDB data analysis by the RoMan team to validate manufacturing enhancements which can minimize creation of manufacturing anomalies.  These actions should culminate, over time, in significantly reduced numbers of manufacturing anomalies.

name: Monte Carlo N Particles
description: MCNP is a general-purpose ionizing radiation modeling software solution developed at Los Alamos National Laboratory for nuclear energy safety applications and weapons modeling. MCNP is distributed by the Radiation Safety Information Computing Center based at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. It is export-controlled software by RSICC because of the software’s potential use in development of nuclear technologies. We will use MCNP to calculate radiation levels at different altitudes. CARI (Civil Aeromedical Research Institute, an older name for the FAA Civil Aeromedical Research Institute) software, developed and distributed by the FAA through its Radiobiology Services website, uses these MCNP-generated data as the basis of calculations of dose rates to occupants of aircraft from Solar and galactic cosmic radiations. Software does need compilation once in a decade to recalibrate radiation levels.

description: The Real Property Geographic Information System (RPGIS) provides a common visual platform for analyzing and reviewing FAA real estate assets within a geographical context, and for visualizing, querying, and referencing the entire US real properties. The solution will be applicable across the Service Areas and Headquarters. The RPGIS makes the data available in a central place for all real estate users. The RPGIS includes features allowing the users to review and filter both FAA leased and owned US property data, based on different layers and factors applied on geographical maps that have data points gathered from different internal FAA databases, other Federal databases, and privately owned databases, and commercial companies. Users have ability to explore data and share location-based insights. The ability to view how real estate and related information is connected, and how the prices of the US real properties are changed will improve decision-making.  RPGIS is a subsystem of RPFMT system.

fullname_0: Performance Data Analysis and Reporting System
description:
The Performance Data Analysis and Reporting System (PDARS) enables analysis of the daily operation of the National Airspace System (NAS) on local, inter-facility and nationwide levels. By translating flight track and flight plan data and integrating that information with other relevant data sources into measures of facility performance, PDARS significantly augments the FAA's ability to adjust operational procedures and techniques. 

PDARS incorporates innovative technology for rapidly processing large volumes of complex air traffic data, for extracting and visualizing information from these data, and for managing a secure network that enables FAA facilities across the continental U.S. to share and discuss this information. Data is accessed daily from all sites, processed overnight, and reports are delivered to all participating facilities routinely each morning.

name: AJW-2 Integrated Business Intelligence System
description:
IBIS leverages Esri ArcGIS map views to depict FAA Corporate Work Plan (CWP) projects and Facility Asset Inventory (FAI) data in a single view to inform NAS infrastructure sustainment planning and analysis activities. IBIS will enable AJW-2 to improve long-term infrastructure sustainment project planning activities and more effectively develop portfolios for inclusion in the infrastructure budget.

IBIS allows users to query data from CWP based on different user defined boundaries or from districts and regions defined within CWP, and numerous programmatic filters. Once projects have been queried, users can view the CWP project schedule information in the Schedule Workbook Sandbox to perform what-if analyses on candidate project schedule changes. The CWP data can also be queried and grouped with FAI asset data including weighted backlog metrics to further optimize NAS sustainment project planning and execution.
